Surat al-Baqarah (The Cow), Medinan, two hundred and eighty-six or eighty-seven verses.

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by this.

**﴿Dhālika﴾** — that, i.e., this **﴿al-Kitāb﴾** (the Book) which Muhammad recites. **﴿Lā rayba﴾** — there is no doubt **﴿fīhi﴾** in it, that it is from Allah. The negated clause is a predicate (khabar) whose subject (mubtada') is **﴿dhālika﴾**, and the demonstrative is used to express magnification. **﴿Hudan﴾** — a second predicate, i.e., a guide, **﴿lil-muttaqīn﴾** — for those who are God-fearing (al-muttaqūn, the ones who arrive at taqwā (God-consciousness) by carrying out the commands (imtithāl al-awāmir) and avoiding the prohibitions (ijtināb al-nawāhī), by which they guard themselves against the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 3:

﴿Those who believe﴾ in (they affirm) ﴿the unseen﴾ that which is hidden from them, namely the Resurrection (al-ba'th), Paradise and Hellfire; ﴿and establish the prayer﴾ i.e., they perform it with its due rights; ﴿and from what We have provided them﴾ We have given them, ﴿they spend﴾ in the obedience of Allah.

﴿And those who believe in what has been sent down to you﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and what was sent down before you﴾, i.e., the Torah, the Gospel and others, ﴿and they are certain of the Hereafter﴾, i.e., they know it.

Those (ʾulāʾika): the ones described by what was mentioned, "upon guidance from their Lord" (ʿalā hudan min rabbihim), "and those are the successful" (wa-ulāʾika humu al-mufliḥūn): the ones who attain victory by Paradise and are saved from the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 6:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾, such as Abu Jahl and Abu Lahab and the like, ﴿it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe﴾. [The two hamzas may be pronounced clearly, or the second may be replaced by an alif, or it may be eased, with an alif inserted between the eased and the other, or left out.] ﴿They will not believe﴾ because God knows from them that this is so, so do not hope for their faith. And warning (indhar) is informing together with frightening.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 7:

﴿Allah has set a seal upon their hearts﴾ He sealed them and made them secure, so that no good enters them. ﴿And upon their hearing﴾ i.e., its places, so that they do not benefit from what they hear of the truth. ﴿And over their eyes is a covering﴾ a veil, so that they do not see the truth. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾ severe and everlasting.

Among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," and it was revealed concerning the hypocrites (al-munafiqun), i.e., the Day of Resurrection, because it is the last of the days. ﴿But they are not believers.﴾ The meaning of "min" (from) was observed in it, and the wording of the pronoun in "yaqul" (says).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti on surah 2, verse 9:

﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe﴾ by showing the opposite of what they conceal of disbelief, so that they may ward off from themselves its worldly rulings. ﴿Yet they deceive none but themselves﴾, because the harm of their deception returns to them, so they are disgraced in this world when Allah informs His Prophet of what they conceal, and they are punished in the Hereafter. ﴿And they are unaware﴾, meaning they do not know that their deception is against themselves. The mukhādaʿa (the mufāʿala form, which denotes reciprocal action) here is from one party, as in ʿāqabtu al-liṣṣ (I punished the thief). Mentioning Allah in it is for embellishment. In another reading it is وما يَخْدَعُونَ (wa-mā yakhdaʿūna, "and they do not deceive"), without the alif.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 10:

﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ doubt and hypocrisy; so it (the disease) makes their hearts sick, i.e., weakens them. ﴿So Allah increased them in disease﴾ by what He sent down of the Qur'an, because of their disbelief in it. ﴿And for them is a painful torment﴾ painful, ﴿because they used to lie﴾ with the doubled (tashdid) pronunciation, i.e., (they lied concerning) the Messenger of Allah; and with the single (takhfif) pronunciation, i.e., their saying "We believe."

And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," (that is, to these people), by disbelief and by hindering others from faith, they say, "We are only reformers." (And what we are engaged in is not corruption.) Allah the Exalted says, refuting them:

Translation:

﴿Ala﴾ is for drawing attention. ﴿Indeed, they are the ones who cause corruption, but they are not aware﴾ of it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 13:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people (the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ) have believed," they say, "Shall we believe as the fools (al-sufaha', the ignorant) have believed?" That is, "We will not do as they do."﴾ Allah the Exalted said in reply to them: ﴿Surely it is they who are the fools, but they do not know.﴾ That [is the end of the verse].

﴿And when they meet﴾: its original form is "laqyū." The damma was dropped for ease of pronunciation (*istithqal*), and then the yā' was dropped because it came together with the silent wāw. ﴿those who believe﴾, they say: ﴿"We believe"﴾. ﴿And when they are alone﴾ away from them ﴿and return to their devils﴾, meaning their leaders, ﴿they say: "Indeed we are with you" in the religion. "We are only mocking"﴾ them by displaying belief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 15:

﴿Allah mocks them﴾ — He requites them for their mockery. ﴿And He leaves them⁠ ﴾ — He gives them respite. ﴿In their transgression﴾ — by their exceeding the limit in disbelief. ﴿They wander blindly﴾ — they waver in bewilderment. (This is a circumstantial clause, ḥāl.)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 16:

﴿Those are the ones who have bought error in exchange for guidance﴾, i.e., they substituted it for it. ﴿So their transaction has not profited﴾, i.e., they did not gain from it; rather, they lost, since they are destined for the Fire, where they will remain forever. ﴿And they were not guided﴾ in what they did.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 17:

﴿Their likeness﴾ means their description in their hypocrisy. ﴿Is like the likeness of one who kindled﴾ lit, kindled (awqada) ﴿a fire﴾ in darkness. ﴿Then when it lit up﴾ illuminated ﴿all around him﴾, he could see, warm himself, and felt safe from what he feared. ﴿God took away their light﴾ extinguished it, and the pronoun is put in the plural in consideration of the meaning of "the one who" (alladhi). ﴿And left them in darkness, unable to see﴾ what is around them, bewildered about the way, fearful. Thus are these people: they felt safe by displaying the word of faith, but when they die, fear and punishment come to them.

They are deaf to the truth, so they do not hear it with an accepting hearing; dumb, mute to good, so they do not speak it; blind to the path of guidance, so they do not see it. "So they will not return" from error.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 19:

﴿Or﴾ their likeness is ﴿like a rainstorm﴾, i.e., like people caught in a rain, and it is originally ṣayyib, from ṣāba yaṣūbu, meaning it descends, ﴿from the sky﴾, meaning the cloud, ﴿in which﴾, i.e., in the cloud, ﴿is darkness﴾ thick and dense, ﴿and thunder﴾, which is the angel entrusted with it, and it is said that it is its sound, ﴿and lightning﴾, the flashing of its sound by which it drives the clouds. ﴿They put their fingers﴾, i.e., the people of the rainstorm, ﴿their fingertips﴾, i.e., their finger tips, ﴿into their ears because of﴾ the ﴿thunderclaps﴾, the intensity of the thunder's sound, lest they hear them, ﴿for fear of﴾, meaning dread of, ﴿death﴾ from hearing them. Likewise these people: when the Qur'an descends, containing mention of disbelief, likened to darkness, and the threat against it, likened to thunder, and the clear proofs, likened to lightning, they stop up their ears lest they hear it and thus incline toward faith and abandon their religion, which to them is death. ﴿And God encompasses the disbelievers﴾ in knowledge and power, so they cannot escape Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 20:

﴿The lightning nearly snatches away their sight﴾ takes them with speed. ﴿Whenever it lights up for them, they walk in it﴾, i.e., in its light. ﴿And when darkness falls over them, they stand still﴾. This is an illustration (tamthil) of how the proofs in the Qur'an disturb their hearts, and of their acceptance of what they hear in it of what they love, and their halting at what they dislike.

﴿If God willed, He would surely take away their hearing﴾, in the sense of their hearing (asma'ihim), ﴿and their sight﴾, the outward ones, just as He took away the inward ones. ﴿Indeed God is All-Powerful over everything﴾ that He wills, and of this is the taking away of what has been mentioned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 21:

﴿O mankind﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿worship﴾ (i.e., affirm the oneness of) ﴿your Lord, who created you﴾ (i.e., brought you into being, when you were nothing) ﴿and those before you﴾ (i.e., created those who came before you), ﴿that you may be mindful [of Him]﴾, by worshipping Him, [and so be protected from] His punishment. As for ﴿la'alla﴾ (perhaps, that you may): originally it expresses hope (tarajji), but in the speech of Allah, the Exalted, it expresses certainty (tahqiq).

﴿Who made﴾ (i.e., created) ﴿for you the earth a bed﴾ (*hal*, a grammatical circumstantial accusative (*ḥāl*), describing the state of "a bed"), a spread-out carpet upon which one lies, neither so hard nor so soft that it would be impossible to settle upon it. ﴿And the sky a structure﴾, a ceiling. ﴿And He sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby﴾ (kinds of) ﴿fruits as provision for you﴾. ﴿So do not set up rivals﴾ (partners) ﴿to God in worship, while you know﴾ that He is the Creator, while you do not create, and that none is a god except the one who creates.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 23:

﴿And if you are in doubt﴾ (i.e., in suspicion) ﴿concerning what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ Muhammad ﴿of the Qur'an, that it is from Allah﴾ ﴿then produce a surah like it﴾, i.e., like what was sent down. The min (from) in "min mithlih" is for explanation (bayan), meaning: it is like it in eloquence (balaghah), excellence of composition (husn al-nazm), and reporting of the unseen (al-ghayb). A surah (surah) is a portion that has a beginning and an end, the least of which is three verses. ﴿And call upon your witnesses﴾ — your gods which you worship ﴿other than Allah﴾, i.e., besides Him, to help you ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that Muhammad said it of his own accord. So do that, for you are Arabs, eloquent like him. When they were unable to do that, the Exalted said:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 24:

﴿And if you do not do it﴾ — that which has been mentioned — due to your inability, ﴿and you will never do it﴾ — that, ever — because of the manifestness of its inimitability. (I'tirad: an interjected clause.) ﴿So fear﴾ — by faith in Allah, and that it is not the speech of humans — ﴿the Fire whose fuel is men﴾ — the disbelievers — ﴿and stones﴾ — like their idols, made of them. He means that it is extremely hot, restricted to what has been mentioned; it is unlike the fire of this world, which is kindled with firewood and the like. ﴿It has been prepared﴾ — readied — ﴿for the disbelievers﴾ — who will be tormented by it. This is a resumptive sentence (jumlah musta'nafah), or a necessary circumstantial clause (hal lazimah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 25:

﴿And give good tidings﴾ inform ﴿those who believe﴾ who affirm belief in Allah ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ of the obligatory (furud) and voluntary (nawafil) acts ﴿that﴾ i.e., that ﴿for them are gardens﴾ orchards with trees and dwellings ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ i.e., beneath their trees and palaces ﴿the rivers﴾ i.e., the waters in them. A nahr (river) is the channel in which water flows, because water digs it out (yanharuhu), i.e., excavates it. Attributing the flowing to the rivers is metaphorical (majaz). ﴿Whenever they are provided with fruit from them﴾ they are fed from those gardens, ﴿as provision﴾ ﴿they will say, "This is what we were provided with before"﴾ i.e., something like what we were provided with before, namely in the Garden, because its fruits resemble one another, as indicated by ﴿and they are given it in similitude﴾ i.e., they are brought the provision ﴿resembling one another﴾, similar to one another in color but differing in taste. ﴿And for them therein are spouses﴾ of the hur (maidens of paradise) and others ﴿purified﴾ from menstruation and every impurity ﴿and therein they will abide forever﴾ remaining eternally, never perishing nor leaving.

It was revealed in response to the statement of the Jews when Allah cited as a parable the fly, in His saying: (And if the fly should snatch away from them anything...) and the spider, in His saying: (like the parable of the spider...). They said: what did Allah intend by mentioning these lowly things? So Allah revealed:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 26:

﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example﴾ (yaḍriba, meaning yajʿal, "to make" or "to set forth"), ﴿a parable﴾ (mathalan), the first object; ﴿what﴾ (mā) is an indefinite noun described by what follows it, serving as the second object, meaning "whatever example it may be"; or it is an extra particle (zāʾida) for emphasizing lowliness, so what follows it is the second object: ﴿a gnat﴾ (baʿūḍa), the singular of baʿūḍ, which is small gnats (ṣighār al-baqq), ﴿or anything above it﴾, meaning larger than it. He does not leave off explaining it because of the ruling it contains.

﴿As for those who believed, they know that it﴾, meaning the parable, ﴿is the truth﴾ (al-ḥaqq), established and placed in its proper position, ﴿from their Lord. As for those who disbelieved, they say: "What did Allah intend by this as a parable?"﴾ (mathalan is a tamyīz, specification, meaning "by this parable"; mā is an interrogative of denial and is the subject (mubtada'), and dhā, meaning alladhī with its relative clause, is the predicate, meaning: what benefit is in it). Allah the Exalted says in answer to them: ﴿By it He causes many to go astray﴾, meaning by this parable, ﴿from the truth, because of their disbelief in it, and by it He guides many﴾ of the believers, ﴿because of their belief in it. And He causes none to go astray by it except the defiantly disobedient﴾ (al-fāsiqīn), those who depart from His obedience.

﴿Alladhīna﴾ (ﷻ) is an adjective (na't) modifying ﴿yanqudūna ʿahda Allāh﴾: what He had covenanted with them in the Scriptures, namely belief in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Min baʿdi mīthāqihi﴾: after its confirmation upon them. ﴿Wa yaqtaʿūna mā amara Allāh bihi an yūṣal﴾: [they sever] what God has commanded to be joined, namely belief in the Prophet, kinship ties (al-raḥim), and other things. ﴿An yūṣal﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in ﴿bihi﴾. ﴿Wa yufsidūna fī al-arḍ﴾: by acts of disobedience and by hindering others from belief. ﴿Ulāʾika﴾: those described by what has been mentioned. ﴿Hum al-khāsirūn﴾: because of their destination to the everlasting Fire upon them.

How can you disbelieve in God, O people of Mecca, when you were dead (ﷺ — i.e., mere drops of semen in the loins) and He gave you life (in the wombs and in this world) by breathing the spirit into you? The interrogative is for the purpose of expressing astonishment at their disbelief despite the presence of proof, or for the purpose of rebuke. Then He will cause you to die when your terms come to an end. Then He will give you life (by resurrection). Then to Him you will be returned, that is, you will be sent back after the resurrection, and He will recompense you for your deeds. And He mentioned (this) as proof of the resurrection, because of what they denied.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 29:

﴿It is He who created for you whatever is on the earth, all of it﴾ i.e., the earth and what is in it, ﴿all of it﴾ so that you may benefit from it and take heed. ﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾ after creating the earth, i.e., He intended to, ﴿and made them complete seven heavens﴾ — the pronoun refers to the heaven because it is in the sense of the clause that leads to it: i.e., He made it, as in another verse (﴿then He completed them as seven heavens﴾), ﴿and He is Knowing of all things﴾, both in summary and in detail. Will you not then take heed, [and realize] that the One who is able to create all that from the beginning, and He is greater than you, is able to restore you?

And mention, O Muhammad, when your Lord said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a khalifah (vicegerent)﴾, who will succeed Me in executing My rulings upon it, and he is Adam. ﴿They said: Will You place upon it one who will cause corruption upon it﴾ through sins ﴿and shed blood﴾ spilling it by killing, as the Banu al-Jann did, and they had been upon it; when they caused corruption, Allah sent the angels against them, and they drove them out to the islands and the mountains. ﴿While we exalt You⁠﻿﻿﻿ with Your praise﴾, meaning we are, while engaged in it, saying "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to Allah). ﴿And sanctify You﴾, meaning we declare You far above what does not befit You. So the lam [in lak] is extra, and the clause is a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: we are more deserving of the vicegerency. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾ of the benefit in appointing Adam, and that among his descendants there will be the obedient and the disobedient, so that justice will become manifest among them. They said: "Our Lord will not create a creation more honored by Him than us, nor more knowledgeable, since we precede them [in worship] and have seen what he has not seen." So Allah Almighty created Adam from the surface of the earth (adim al-ard), meaning its face, by taking a handful from all its colors, and it was kneaded with various waters, and He fashioned him, breathed into him the spirit, and he became a sentient living being after having been inanimate matter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 31:

﴿And He taught Adam the names﴾, i.e., the names of the things named, ﴿all of them﴾, by casting knowledge of them into his heart. ﴿Then He presented them﴾, i.e., the things named, and in this there is the predominance of rational beings (taghlib al-'uqala'), ﴿to the angels, and said﴾ to them, as a rebuke, ﴿"Inform Me﴾, tell Me ﴿of the names of these﴾, the things named, ﴿if you are truthful"﴾ in your claim that I do not create anyone more knowledgeable than you, or that you are more deserving of the vicegerency (khilafah). The answer to the conditional clause is indicated by what precedes it.

They said, "Glory be to You!" — exalting You above being questioned — "We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise," the Who nothing escapes from His knowledge and wisdom.

"He said, [Allah] the Exalted: "O Adam, inform them of their names." That is, of the angels, "of their names," meaning the named things. So he named everything by its name, and mentioned the wisdom for which it was created. "So when he had informed them of their names, He said," the Exalted, rebuking them: "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth," meaning what is hidden in them, "and I know what you reveal," meaning what you make apparent of your statement, "Will You place in it...", "and what you were concealing," meaning what you keep secret of your statement, "He will not create one more honored by Him than us, nor more knowing."

(And) remember when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," a prostration of greeting by bowing. So they prostrated, except Iblis. He was the father of the jinn, and he was among the angels. He refused (abā), i.e., declined to prostrate, and grew arrogant (wa-staksara), i.e., became proud against it, and said, "I am better than him," and he was among the disbelievers (al-kāfirīn) in the knowledge of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 35:

﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden"﴾ "You" (أنْت) is an emphasis (*tawkid*, reinforcing a word for clarity or stress) on the concealed pronoun (*al-damir al-mustatir*, the pronoun understood within the verb "dwell"), so that "your wife" can be conjoined to it. "Your wife" (زوجك) refers to Ḥawwā' (Eve), pronounced with the *madd* (the lengthened vowel). He had created her from his left rib. ﴿and the Garden, and eat from it freely﴾, meaning eat abundantly, with no restriction, ﴿wherever you both wish, but do not approach this tree﴾, meaning by eating from it. It is wheat, or the grapevine, or something else. ﴿Lest you become among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning the disobedient.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 36:

﴿فَأَزَلَّهُما الشَّيْطان﴾ Iblis caused them to slip, i.e., he made them go away. In another reading, ﴿فَأَزالهُما﴾ (fa-azālahumā), he removed them, ﴿عَنْها﴾ from it, i.e., from the Garden, by saying to them: "Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and to a kingdom that does not decay?" and he swore to them by Allah that he was surely one of those who give sincere advice to them. So they ate from it. ﴿فَأَخْرَجَهُما مِمّا كانا فِيهِ﴾ He expelled them from what they had been in, namely the bliss. ﴿وقُلْنا اهْبِطُوا﴾ And We said: Go down to the earth, i.e., you two together with what your offspring contain of your progeny, ﴿بَعْضكُمْ﴾ some of you, some of the offspring, ﴿لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوّ﴾ are enemies to others, through the wrongdoing of some of you toward others. ﴿ولَكُمْ فِي الأَرْض مُسْتَقَرّ﴾ And for you on the earth is a place of settlement, ﴿ومَتاع﴾ and enjoyment of what you benefit from of its plants, ﴿إلى حِين﴾ until a time, i.e., the time when your terms come to an end.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 37:

﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾ (Allah) inspired him with them. In another reading, Adam is in the accusative (manṣūb) and "words" in the nominative (marfū'), meaning: they came to him. They were: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾, and the verse [continues]. So he supplicated with them. ﴿So He accepted his repentance﴾: He accepted his repentance. ﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance﴾ toward His servants, ﴿the Merciful﴾ to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 38:

﴿We said: "Go down from it"﴾ from the Garden, ﴿all of you﴾. He repeated it so that what follows could be joined to it. ﴿Then, if﴾ there is an assimilation here of the conditional particle nūn of in (in) into the superfluous mā, ﴿there comes to you from Me guidance﴾, a Book and a Messenger, ﴿then whoever follows My guidance﴾, believing in Me and acting in obedience to Me, ﴿no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾ in the Hereafter, by their entering the Garden.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 39:

﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs﴾ — Our books — ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally﴾ — remaining forever, never perishing and never coming out.

O Children of Israel (the descendants of Ya'qub/Jacob), remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, i.e., upon your forefathers: the deliverance from Fir'awn (Pharaoh), the splitting of the sea, the shading of the clouds, and other things, by thanking Me through obedience to Me. And fulfil My covenant which I covenanted with you, namely belief in Muhammad; I will fulfil your covenant, namely the reward for it by entry into Paradise. And fear Me alone, so dread Me in abandoning the fulfilment of it, not anyone else.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 41:

﴿And believe in what I have sent down﴾ of the Qur'an, ﴿confirming what is with you﴾ of the Torah, by its agreement with it concerning monotheism (tawhid) and prophethood, ﴿and do not be the first to disbelieve in it﴾ among the People of the Book, for those after you follow you, so their sin will be upon you. ﴿And do not exchange﴾ meaning, do not substitute ﴿My signs﴾ which are in your scripture, concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿for a small price﴾ a meager, fleeting gain of this world. That is: do not conceal them out of fear of losing what you take from your common people. ﴿And fear Me, and Me alone﴾ be wary of Me in this matter, not other than Me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 42:

﴿And do not mix﴾ (talbisu, i.e. do not confuse or mingle) ﴿the truth﴾ which I have sent down to you ﴿with falsehood﴾ which you fabricate ﴿and﴾ do not ﴿conceal the truth﴾, the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿while you know﴾ that it is the truth.

﴿And establish prayer, give zakat (obligatory alms), and bow with those who bow.﴾ Pray with those who pray: Muhammad and his Companions. It was revealed concerning their scholars, who used to say to their Muslim relatives, "Remain steadfast upon the religion of Muhammad, for it is true."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 44:

﴿Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people﴾ — i.e., faith in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿and forget yourselves﴾ — you leave them [unenjoined], so you do not command them to it. ﴿while you recite the Book?﴾ — the Torah, in which there is a warning against saying one thing and doing another. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ — [to understand] the evil of your conduct, so that you would turn back. So the clause "and forget yourselves" is the place of the rhetorical question of rebuke (al-istifham al-inkari).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 45:

﴿And seek help﴾ ask for assistance in your affairs ﴿through patience﴾ restraining the self from what it dislikes ﴿and prayer﴾ he singled it out for mention, magnifying its status. And in a hadith: (When a matter distressed him, the Prophet (ﷺ) would hasten to prayer). It is also said that the address is to the Jews, since greed and love of leadership had hindered them from faith; so they were commanded to be patient, which is fasting, because it breaks desire, and to pray, because it produces humility (khushu') and removes arrogance. ﴿And indeed it﴾ i.e., prayer ﴿is burdensome﴾ heavy ﴿except for the humble﴾ those who are calm and inclined to obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 46:

﴿Who are certain (yuqinun) that﴾ they will meet their Lord, [meaning] by resurrection, ﴿and that to Him they will return﴾ in the Hereafter, so that He will recompense them.

O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you, by being thankful for it through obedience to Me, and that I preferred you over the worlds, i.e., your forefathers, over the peoples of their time.

﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ *(Wat-taqu)*: fear ﴿يَوْمًا﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿لَا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ *(on which no soul will avail another soul in anything)*. ﴿لَا تَجْزِي﴾ *(will not avail)* in it ﴿نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾.

﴿وَلَا يُقْبَلُ﴾ *(nor will be accepted)*, read with the *ta'* (ﺕ) or the *ya'* (ﻱ), ﴿مِنْهَا شَفَاعَةٌ﴾ *(from it any intercession)*, meaning: it will have no intercession that would be accepted.

﴿فَمَا لَنَا مِنْ شَافِعِينَ﴾ *(So we have no intercessors)*.

﴿عَدْلٌ﴾ *('adl)*: ransom.

﴿وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ *(nor will they be helped)*: they will be prevented from the punishment of God.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 49:

﴿And﴾ remember ﴿when We delivered you﴾ — i.e., your forefathers. The address, both here and in what follows, is to those present in the time of our Prophet, concerning what Allah bestowed upon their forefathers, as a reminder to them of Allah's blessing, ﴿so that you might believe﴾. ﴿From the people of Pharaoh, who were inflicting upon you﴾ — making you taste — ﴿the worst torment﴾, its most severe form. The clause is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun in "We delivered you." ﴿They slaughtered﴾ is an explanation (bayān) of what precedes it: ﴿your sons﴾, those who were born, ﴿and spared your women﴾ — ﴿spared﴾ meaning kept alive — ﴿your women﴾, because some of the soothsayers (kahana) had said to him: "A boy will be born among the Children of Israel who will be the cause of the loss of your kingdom." ﴿And in that﴾ — the torment or the deliverance — ﴿was a trial﴾ (balā', i.e., an ordeal) ﴿or a blessing﴾ (in'ām) ﴿from your Lord, a great one.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 50:

﴿And﴾ remember [when] ﴿We parted﴾ (faraqna), i.e., split (falaqna), ﴿the sea for you﴾ (bikum), i.e., because of you, ﴿the sea﴾, until you entered it fleeing from your enemy, ﴿and We saved you﴾ from drowning, ﴿and We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾, his people along with him, ﴿while you were looking on﴾ at the sea closing over them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 51:

﴿And [remember] when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights﴾ with an alif and other than it, ﴿forty nights﴾ — We would give him at the end of them the Torah so that you might act by it. ﴿Then you took the calf﴾ which the Samiri fashioned for you ﴿as a god after him﴾, i.e., after his departure to Our appointment, ﴿while you were wrongdoers﴾ by taking it, because you placed worship in other than its proper place.
[Qur'an 2:52] "Then We pardoned you after that" — we erased your sins — "after that," i.e., after the taking (of the calf as a deity), "that you might be grateful" — for Our blessing upon you.

And when We gave Moses the Book — the Torah — and the Criterion (al-Furqan), an explanatory conjunction, meaning that which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between the lawful and the unlawful, ﴿so that you might be guided﴾ by it away from error.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 54:

﴿And when Moses said to his people﴾ — those who worshipped the calf — ﴿"O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf"﴾ — "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf as a god." ﴿So repent to your Creator﴾ — your Creator (khaliq), by ceasing to worship Him [i.e., the calf] ﴿and kill yourselves﴾ — meaning, let the innocent among you kill the guilty ﴿That is best for you with your Creator﴾ — so He enabled you to do that, and He sent over you a black cloud so that some of you could not see others, and so one would not pity his kinsman, until about seventy thousand of you were killed ﴿Then He accepted your repentance﴾ — He accepted your repentance ﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾

﴿And when you said﴾ while you had set out with Moses to seek forgiveness from Allah for worshipping the calf, and you had heard His speech, ﴿"O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah plainly"﴾ openly, face to face, ﴿so the thunderbolt seized you﴾ the cry, and you died, ﴿while you were looking on﴾ at what had befallen you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 56:

﴿Then We raised you﴾ We gave you life ﴿after your death, that perhaps you might be grateful﴾ that perhaps you might be grateful for Our blessing by that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 57:

﴿And We shaded you with the clouds,﴾ We screened you with thin clouds from the heat of the sun in the wilderness (al-tih). ﴿And We sent down upon you﴾ therein ﴿the manna and the quail.﴾ They are the taranjabin (manna, a sweet exudation) and the quail (al-salwa), with the mim lightened and the alif shortened (al-qasr). And We said: ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you,﴾ and do not store them up. But they were ungrateful for the blessing, and they stored them up, so He cut it off from them. ﴿And they did not wrong Us﴾ by that, ﴿but they were wronging themselves,﴾ because its harm fell upon them.

﴿And when We said﴾ to them, after their emergence from the wandering (al-tih, the desert wilderness in which they were lost), ﴿Enter this town﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) or Ariha (Jericho), ﴿and eat from it wherever you wish, in abundance﴾, meaning widely, without restriction, ﴿and enter the gate﴾, i.e., its gate, ﴿prostrating﴾, meaning bowing low, ﴿and say﴾, meaning, our request is, ﴿"Hittah"﴾, i.e., that You remove our sins from us, ﴿and We will forgive you your sins﴾. In another recitation (qira'ah), it is read with the yā' and with the tā' (in the first person and second person forms), both in the passive form (mabniyyan li-l-maf'ul, "مَبْنِيًّا لِلْمَفْعُولِ"), in both of them. ﴿And We will increase those who do good﴾ in obedience with reward.

﴿So those who did wrong among them substituted a saying other than what had been said to them﴾, and they said: "A grain in a hair" (*ḥabbah fī shaʿrah*), and they entered crawling on their backsides (*astāhihim*). ﴿So We sent down upon those who did wrong﴾. Here the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun (*waḍʿ al-ẓāhir mawḍiʿ al-muḍmar*), for emphasis in condemning their condition. ﴿a punishment (*rijz*)﴾, meaning a plague (*ṭāʿūn*), ﴿from the heaven, because they were defiantly disobeying﴾, meaning because of their defiance, that is, their departure from obedience. So there died of them in one hour seventy thousand, or fewer.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 60:

﴿And﴾ mention "when Moses asked for water for his people" ﴿i.e., he requested water﴾ "while they were parched with thirst in the wilderness" ﴿of Sinai, a wilderness of wandering (al-tih)﴾. "So We said: Strike the rock with your staff." ﴿And it was a light, square-shaped stone, like a man's head, of marble or of granite (kadhdhan)﴾ "and he struck it" ﴿so it split and flowed﴾ "and there gushed forth from it twelve springs" ﴿according to the number of the tribes (al-asbat)﴾. "Each people knew its drinking place" ﴿each tribe (sibt) among them knew its place of drinking, so that no one else would share it with them﴾. "And We said: Eat and drink of God's provision, and do not go about in the earth spreading corruption" ﴿this is a emphatic circumstantial clause (hal), whose governing verb is from ʿathiya, with the ṯāʾ kasrah, meaning "to corrupt"﴾.

﴿And when you said, "Moses, we will not endure one kind of food"﴾, i.e., one kind of it, ﴿"which is the manna and quail"﴾. ﴿"So call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us"﴾ something ﴿"of what the earth grows: its herbs"﴾, its ﴿"cucumbers, garlic, lentils and onions."﴾ Its wheat. ﴿He said﴾, Moses said to them, ﴿"Would you exchange what is lower"﴾, what is baser, ﴿"for what is better?"﴾, what is nobler? Would you take it in its place? The hamza here is for rebuke. They refused to return, so he called upon God Most High, and He said, Most High, ﴿"Go down"﴾, descend ﴿"into a town"﴾ of the towns, ﴿"for you will have there"﴾ ﴿"what you asked for"﴾ of plants. ﴿"And humiliation and wretchedness were stamped upon them"﴾, meaning abasement and disgrace. ﴿"Wretchedness"﴾ means the trace of poverty, from being stilled and disgraced. It clings to them, even if they are rich, just as the minted dirham clings to its stamp. ﴿"And they returned"﴾, went back, ﴿"with anger from God. That"﴾, i.e., the stamping and the anger, ﴿"is because they"﴾, i.e., because of the fact that ﴿"they disbelieved in God's signs and killed the prophets"﴾, such as Zakariyya and Yahya, ﴿"without right"﴾, i.e., wrongfully. ﴿"That is because they disobeyed and were transgressors,"﴾ exceeding the limit in acts of disobedience. He repeated it for emphasis.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 62:

﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾ in the prophets before [Muhammad] ﴿and those who were Jews﴾, they are the Jews, ﴿and the Christians and the Sabians﴾, a sect from among the Jews or the Christians, ﴿whoever believed﴾ among them ﴿in Allah and the Last Day﴾ during the time of our Prophet ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾ according to his law, ﴿they will have their reward﴾, that is, the reward of their deeds, ﴿with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. The pronoun in "believed" and "did" takes account of the wording of "whoever" (man), and what follows it takes account of its meaning.

And remember (when We took your covenant) your pledge to act upon what is in the Torah, and (when We raised over you the Mount) Tur, (that is, We uprooted the mountain from its base and held it over you) because you refused to accept it. And We said: "Take what We have given you with strength," with earnestness and diligence, "and remember what is in it," by acting upon it, "so that you may be God-fearing" (taqwa), (that is, that you may guard yourselves against) the Fire, or against sins.

Then you turned away (ʾaʿraḍtum) after that (al-mīthāq, the covenant) from obedience, ﴿and had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy﴾ to you, by granting repentance or by postponing the punishment, ﴿you would have been among the losers﴾, the ruined.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 65:

﴿And indeed you have known﴾ (lam of oath) ﴿those of you who transgressed concerning the Sabbath﴾ (i.e., they exceeded the limit) by hunting fish, although We had forbidden them from it; and they were the people of Aylah (Eilat). ﴿So We said to them: "Be apes, despised and repelled."﴾ (mub'adin, i.e., expelled). So they became such, and they perished after three days.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 66:

﴿So We made it﴾ i.e., that punishment, ﴿a deterrent﴾ (nakal), a lesson preventing the commission of the like of what they did, ﴿for what lay before it and what lay behind it﴾, i.e., for the nations of its time and those after it, ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ (muttaqin) of Allah. They were singled out for mention because they are the ones who benefit from it, unlike others.

[And] mention ﴿when Musa said to his people﴾, after a man had been killed among them and his killer was unknown. They asked him to supplicate Allah to make the killer clear to them, so he supplicated [Allah]. ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.﴾ They said: ﴿Do you take us for a laughingstock?﴾ meaning, mocking us, since you answer us with the like of that. ﴿He said: I seek refuge﴾ I refrain ﴿in Allah from being among the ignorant﴾, the mockers.

When they realized that he was resolute, they said, "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is," meaning: what its age is. He said, "Indeed He says, it is a cow neither old (fārid) that is past its prime, nor a young virgin (bikr), but middle-aged (ʿawān) between those, that is, between the ages mentioned. So do what you are commanded," namely, slaughter it.

They said, "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what its color is." He said, "Indeed He says it is a yellow cow, bright in its yellowness, pleasing to the observers."

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿They said, "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what its color is." He said, "Indeed He says it is a yellow cow, bright of its color, pleasing to those who look upon it."﴾

Note on the gloss: "fāqi' lawnuhā" (فاقِع لَوْنها) means intensely bright in its color, i.e. very deep yellow, and "tasurr al-nāẓirīn" (تَسُرّ النّاظِرِينَ) means it pleases the onlookers, that is, it delights them by its beauty, meaning it gladdens them.

They said, "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what she is," (i.e., whether she is grazing freely or used for work). "Indeed, the cow (i.e., its species, described by what was mentioned) has become confused for us" because of its multiplicity, so we have not been guided to the one intended. "And indeed we, if God wills, will surely be guided" to her.

And in a hadith: "Had they not made the exception (saying 'if God wills'), they would never have had it made clear to them until the end of time."

ﷻ "He said, 'He says it is a cow neither broken to plough the earth nor to water the tilled field, sound, with no blemish on it.'"

﴿قالَ إنّهُ يَقُول إنّها بَقَرَة لا ذَلُول﴾ (He said, "Indeed He says, it is a cow, not broken [ dhalūl ]") — not tamed by work — ﴿تُثِير الأَرْض﴾ ("that plows up the earth") — it turns it over for cultivation. The clause describing it, "dhalūl," is included within the prohibition (al-nahy). ﴿ولا تَسْقِي الحَرْث﴾ ("nor waters the tilled field") — the land prepared for cultivation. ﴿مُسَلَّمَة﴾ ("sound") — free from defects and the traces of work. ﴿لا شِيَة﴾ ("with no blemish") — no color ﴿فِيها﴾ ("on it") other than its own color.

﴿قالُوا الآن جِئْت بِالحَقِّ﴾ ("They said, 'Now you have brought the truth'") — you have spoken with complete clarity. So they searched for it and found it with a young man who was dutiful to his mother, and they bought it for its weight in gold (bi-milʾ mishkihā dhahaban). ﴿فَذَبَحُوها وما كادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ ("So they slaughtered it, though they nearly did not") — because of its high price.

In a hadith: "If they had slaughtered any cow at all, it would have sufficed them, but they made it difficult for themselves, so Allah made it difficult for them."

﴿And when you killed a soul and then disputed over it﴾. Here there is idgham (assimilation) of the dāl into the tā' in فادّارَأْتُمْ, meaning تَخاصَمْتُمْ وتَدافَعْتُمْ, "you disputed and repelled one another." ﴿Concerning it, and Allah would bring out﴾, i.e. manifest, ﴿what you were concealing﴾ regarding its matter. This is a parenthetical interjection (i'tirāḍ), and it is the beginning of the story.

﴿So We said: "Strike him with part of it"﴾, meaning the slain man. [They] struck him with its tongue, or with its tailbone, and he came back to life and said: "So-and-so and so-and-so killed me," referring to his two paternal cousins. Then he died, and they were deprived of the inheritance and were killed. The verse does not specify which part of the cow the slain man was struck with so that he would live. It is not for us to specify it except by a sound, reliable report. To specify it without a chain of transmission (sanad) is mere conjecture (takharrus), because the apparent meaning of the verse is that whichever part of the cow the slain man was struck with, it restored life to him and he named his killer. ﴿Thus﴾, that is, this kind of reviving, ﴿God brings the dead to life and shows you His signs﴾, the proofs of His power, ﴿so that you may understand﴾, that is, reflect, so that you will know that the One who is able to revive one soul is able to revive many souls, and so that you will believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 74:

﴿Then your hearts hardened﴾, O Jews, became hard (ṣalabat) in accepting the truth, ﴿after that﴾, referring to what was mentioned of the reviving of the slain man and the other signs before it, ﴿so they were like stones﴾ in hardness, ﴿or harder in hardness﴾ than them. ﴿And indeed among stones there are those from which rivers gush forth, and indeed among them there are those that split open﴾ — here the ta' (of yatashaqqaq, originally) is assimilated into the shin (idgham) — ﴿so water comes out from them, and indeed among them there are those that fall down﴾, that is, descend from a height to a lower place, ﴿out of fear of Allah﴾. And your hearts are not affected, nor soften, nor humble themselves. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾; He only delays you until your appointed time. And in another reading it is read with the yā' (bi-l-taḥtāniyya, the third person), and in it there is a shift (iltifāt) from direct address to third-person reference.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 75:

﴿Do you (believers) hope﴾ — the hamza here is for denial, meaning: do not hope, for they have a prior record of disbelief — ﴿that they will believe for you﴾, i.e., the Jews, ﴿while a group of them﴾ — a party — ﴿among them﴾, their rabbis, ﴿used to hear the Word of Allah﴾ in the Torah, ﴿then they distorted it﴾, changing it, ﴿after they had understood it﴾, comprehended it, ﴿and they knew﴾ that they were fabricators.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 2, verse 76:**

﴿When they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe."﴾ That is, the hypocrites among the Jews. [They say, "We believe"] that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a Prophet, and that he is the one foretold in our Scripture. ﴿But when they are alone, some of them with others, they say﴾ That is, their leaders, who did not become hypocrites, say to those who did: ﴿"Do you speak to them"﴾ That is, the believers ﴿"of what Allah has disclosed to you?"﴾ That is, "what He made known to you in the Torah concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ)." ﴿"So that they may argue against you before your Lord with it"﴾ That is, so that they may dispute with you. The *lam* here is *lam al-sayrurah* (the lam of consequence, indicating a result that follows, rather than an intended purpose). ﴿"Before your Lord"﴾ on the Day of Judgment, ﴿and so that they may establish the proof against you for not following him, although you know of his truthfulness."﴾ ﴿"Do you not then reason?"﴾ That is, do you not understand that they will argue against you if you speak to them, so that you would stop doing so?

Allah says: ﴿Do they not know﴾ The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir), and the waw that precedes it is for coordination (ʿatf). ﴿That Allah knows what they conceal and what they disclose﴾ what they hide and what they show of that and other than it, so that they would refrain from that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 78:

﴿And among them﴾, i.e., the Jews, ﴿are unlettered (ummiyyun)﴾, common people, ﴿who do not know the Book﴾, the Torah, ﴿except⁠﴾ but only ﴿wishful fancies (amani)﴾, lies that they received from their leaders and accepted as authoritative. ﴿And they are not﴾, in denying the prophethood of the Prophet and other matters that they fabricate, ﴿except that they conjecture﴾, merely conjecturing, and they have no knowledge.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 79:

﴿So woe﴾ means severe punishment, ﴿to those who write the Book with their own hands﴾, i.e., fabricated by themselves, ﴿then say, "This is from Allah," that they may exchange it for a small price﴾ from the worldly life. They are the Jews, who altered the description of the Prophet in the Torah, the verse of stoning, and other things, and wrote them contrary to what was revealed. ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written﴾ of the fabricated text, ﴿and woe to them for what they earn﴾ of bribes; rishā is the plural of rishwah (bribe).

**﴿And they said﴾**, when the Prophet had promised them the Fire: **﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾**, few, namely forty days, the period of their fathers' worship of the calf, after which it will cease. **﴿Say﴾** to them, O Muhammad: **﴿Have you taken with Allah a covenant﴾**, a binding pledge from Him to that effect? The connecting hamza (*hamzat al-wasl*, the hamza pronounced only at the beginning of speech) in *atakhadtum* has been dropped, because the interrogative hamza (*hamzat al-istifham*, the hamza of questioning) takes its place. **﴿Then Allah will not break His covenant﴾** with you? No. **﴿Or⦆** (*am*, meaning "rather"), **﴿you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾**

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 81:

﴿Yes [the Fire will touch you, and you will remain in it forever]﴾ ﴿Whoever earns an evil deed﴾, [i.e., polytheism] ﴿and whose sin has encompassed him﴾ — read in both the singular and the plural (khati'atuhu / khati'atuhum) — meaning it has overpowered him and surrounded him from every side, by his dying as a polytheist, ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾. Here the meaning of "man" (min) has been observed.

Mention (ﷺ) when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel [in the Torah], and We said, ﴿You shall not worship except Allah﴾. This is a statement in the sense of a prohibition (khabar bi-ma'na al-nahy). It is also read as "lā ta'budū" (do not worship). The verb "ta'budūn" is read with the taa' (second person) and with the yaa' (third person).

﴿And [be good] to parents﴾, [and do] ﴿good﴾ [to them], meaning dutifulness, ﴿and to the kinsfolk﴾, meaning relatives, coordinated (ʿatf) with "parents", ﴿and orphans, and the needy. And speak to people﴾ ﴿kindly﴾, meaning commanding what is right, forbidding what is wrong, speaking truthfully about Muhammad, and being gentle with them. It is also read with a ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and a sukūn on the sīn (ḥusn), a verbal noun used as an adjective for emphasis (mubālaghah). ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾, so you accepted that. ﴿Then you turned away﴾, meaning you turned away from fulfilling it. Here there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person (ghaybah) [to the second person]. The intended people are their forefathers. ﴿Except a few of you, and you are [habitually] averse﴾ to it, like your forefathers.

And when We took your covenant: "Do not shed your blood (ﷺ—no)..."

Let me correct that and give the translation properly:

And when We took your covenant, and [said]: "Do not shed your blood," meaning do not spill it by killing one another; "and do not expel yourselves from your homes," meaning do not let one another be driven out of their homes. "Then you acknowledged," i.e., you accepted that covenant, "and you were witnesses" against yourselves.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 85:

﴿Then you are those﴾ O ﴿who kill yourselves﴾ by killing one another ﴿and expel a group of you from their homes, supporting [one another] against them﴾ in sin. The tā' in the original form (tatazāharūn) is assimilated into the ẓā' (idghām), and in a reading with the tā' lightened by deletion, it is tataʿāwarūn (you cooperate) ﴿against them in sinfulness﴾ in disobedience ﴿and transgression﴾ injustice. ﴿And if they come to you as captives﴾ in another reading, ʾusrā ﴿you ransom them﴾ (tufādūhum), in the original tafdūhum, and in another reading tufādhuhum, meaning you rescue them from captivity with wealth or otherwise, and this is among what was enjoined upon you. ﴿Yet it is forbidden for you to expel them﴾ — this is connected to His words "and you expel", and the sentence between them is a parenthetical interjection: that is, just as abandoning ransom was forbidden, so too was expulsion. The tribe of Qurayẓah had allied with the Aws, and the Naḍīr with the Khazraj, so each party would fight alongside its allies, ravage their homes and expel them. When they were taken captive, they would ransom them. When they were asked, "Why do you fight them and ransom them?" they would say, "We have been commanded to ransom," and it would be said, "Then why do you fight them?" They would reply, out of shame, "lest our allies be humiliated." ﴿Do you then believe in part of the Book﴾ which is the ransom ﴿and disbelieve in part﴾ which is the abandonment of killing, expulsion and support. ﴿So what is the recompense of those who do that except disgrace﴾ humiliation and abasement ﴿in the life of this world﴾. They were indeed disgraced by the killing of Qurayẓah, the banishment of the Naḍīr to Syria, and the imposition of the jizyah. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾ — read as yaʿmalūn (with yā') and taʿmalūn (with tā').

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 86:

﴿Those are the ones who have bought the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter⦆ by preferring it over it. ﴿So the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped⦆ they will be prevented from it.

And We certainly gave Moses the Book (*al-Kitab*), meaning the Torah (*al-Tawrah*). ﴿And We followed up after him with messengers﴾, meaning We made messengers follow one another, one messenger after another. ﴿And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, the clear proofs﴾, meaning the miracles, such as raising the dead, and healing the one born blind and the leper. ﴿And We strengthened him﴾, meaning We supported him, ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾. This is an *idafa* (construct phrase, where a noun is annexed to a following noun) in which the qualified is annexed to its qualifier, meaning the holy spirit, namely Gabriel (*Jibril*), who was pure, and who travelled with him wherever he went. ﴿Then, whenever a messenger came to you with what you did not desire﴾, meaning what you did not love, ﴿for your souls﴾, from the truth, ﴿you became arrogant﴾, meaning you were proud and refused to follow him. The answer to *kullama* (whenever) is this clause, and the interrogative sense is its place, and what is meant by it is reproach. ﴿So a party﴾ of them ﴿you denied﴾, like Jesus, ﴿and a party you kill﴾. The present tense (*al-mudari'*) is used to narrate a past situation (*hikayat al-hal*), meaning you killed, like Zechariah (*Zakariyya*) and John (*Yahya*).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 88:

﴿And they say﴾ to the Prophet, mockingly, ﴿"Our hearts are uncovered (ghulf)"﴾. Ghulf is the plural of aghlaf, meaning covered over with coverings, so they do not understand what you say. ﴿Rather﴾ (bal) is used for retraction (al-idrab), ﴿Allah has cursed them﴾, i.e., removed them far from His mercy and forsaken them from accepting, ﴿because of their disbelief﴾. Their non-acceptance is not due to a defect in their hearts. ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾: ma is a superfluous particle (za'ida) for emphasizing the scarcity, i.e., their faith is very little.

And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, [i.e.,] from the Torah, [which is] the Qur'an, **and before its coming** they had been **seeking victory** (*yastaftihuna*, i.e., *yastansirun*) **over those who disbelieved**, saying: "O Allah, grant us victory over them through the Prophet who will be sent at the end of time." **But when there came to them what they recognized** of the truth, which is the sending of the Prophet, **they disbelieved in him**, out of envy and fear for their leadership. The answer to the first *lamma* (*lamma al-ula*) is indicated by the answer to the second (*jawab al-thaniya*): **"So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers."**

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 90:

﴿Wretched is that for which they sold﴾ (bi'sama ishtaraw) — they sold; "mā" here is indefinite, meaning "shay'an" (a thing), an specification (tamyiz) for the subject of "bi'sa" (wretched), and the one singled out for censure is ﴿themselves﴾ (bihi anfusahum), i.e., their share of reward.

﴿That they disbelieve﴾ (an yakfurū), i.e., their disbelief ﴿in what Allah has sent down﴾ (bimā anzala Allāh), namely the Qur'an, ﴿out of spite﴾ (baghyan) — an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu) for "yakfurū": i.e., out of envy ﴿that Allah should send down﴾ (an yunazzila Allāh), read with light and heavy (tashdīd) forms of the verb, ﴿of His bounty﴾ (min faḍlihi), the revelation, ﴿upon whomever He wills﴾ (ʿalā man yashāʾu) for the mission, ﴿of His servants. So they returned﴾ (fa-bāʾū), i.e., they went back ﴿with wrath﴾ (bi-ghaḍabin) from Allah, because of their disbelief in what was sent down; and the indefiniteness is for magnification (taʿẓīm), ﴿upon wrath﴾ (ʿalā ghaḍab) which they had deserved before, by squandering the Torah and disbelieving in ʿĪsā. ﴿And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment﴾ (ʿadhābun muhīn), i.e., one possessing humiliation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 91:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down,"﴾ [meaning] the Qur'an and other than it, ﴿they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us,"﴾ i.e., the Torah, ﴿and they reject what is beyond it,﴾ i.e., other than it, or what comes after it of the Qur'an. ﴿while it is the truth﴾ (a circumstantial clause, ḥāl), ﴿confirming﴾ (a second circumstantial clause, emphasizing the first) ﴿what is with them.﴾ Say [to them], ﴿"Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾ i.e., you killed them, ﴿if you were believers﴾ in the Torah, and in it you were forbidden to kill them. The address is to those existing in the time of our Prophet, [held responsible] for what their forefathers did, because of their approval of it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 92:

﴿And Moses certainly came to you with the clear proofs﴾ — with the miracles, such as the staff, the hand, and the splitting of the sea. ﴿Then you took the calf﴾ — as a god ﴿after him﴾ — after his departure to the appointed time. ﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾ — by taking it.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on Surah al-Baqarah (2), verse 93:

﴿And when We took your covenant﴾ to act upon what is in the Torah, ﴿and﴾ [We had] ﴿raised Mount Tur above you﴾, the mountain, when you refused to accept it, so that it would fall upon you. And We said: ﴿Take what We have given you with strength﴾, with earnestness and diligence, ﴿and listen﴾ to what you are commanded, listening with acceptance. ﴿They said: We have heard﴾ your word ﴿and we disobeyed﴾ your command. ﴿And they were made to drink the calf into their hearts﴾, meaning its love mixed into their hearts the way drink mixes [with what it is in]. ﴿Because of their disbelief. Say﴾ to them: ﴿Wretched is what your faith commands you﴾, namely the worship of the calf, ﴿if you are believers﴾ in it, as you claim. The meaning is: you are not believers, because faith does not command worship of the calf. The intended ones are their forefathers, i.e., likewise you are not believers in the Torah, since you have denied Muhammad, and belief in it does not command denying him.

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿If the Last Abode﴾, meaning Paradise, is ﴿with Allah exclusively﴾, meaning specifically yours, ﴿to the exclusion of the people﴾, ﴿as you claim﴾, ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾. The two conditions are linked to "wish for death," with the first serving as a qualifier of the second. That is: if you are truthful in your claim that it is yours, and whoever it belongs to prefers it, and what conveys one to it is death, then wish for death.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 95:

﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forward﴾ from their disbelief in the Prophet, which entails their lying, ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, the disbelievers, so He will recompense them.

And you will surely find them (the Jews) the most eager of people for life, and (more eager) than those who associate partners with God. Each one of them wishes he could be given a life of a thousand years; (the particle) law here is verbal (masdariyya), meaning "that", and with its clause it is in the sense of a verbal noun, the object of yawaddu (wishes). Yet it will not remove him from the punishment (the Fire) that he be granted long life; (the pronoun in) huwa is for ahadahum ("one of them"), the subject of muzahzihi (one who removes/distances him), meaning his being granted life. And God is Seer of what they do, read with ya' and with ta' (both readings), so He will recompense them.

Ibn Suriya asked the Prophet (ﷺ), or Umar, about which of the angels brings the revelation. He said, "Gabriel." He said, "He is our enemy; he brings punishment. If it had been Michael, we would have believed, for he brings fertility and peace." So it was revealed:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Jibril﴾, then let him die of rage, ﴿for indeed he has brought it down﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿upon your heart by the permission﴾, by the command, ﴿of Allah, confirming what is before it﴾, meaning the books revealed before it, ﴿and a guidance﴾ from error, ﴿and good tidings﴾ of Paradise ﴿for the believers﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 98:

﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, and Jibreel (Gabriel)﴾ with the jeem vowelled with kasra and with fatha, without a hamza, and with a yaa' and without it. ﴿And Mikaal (Michael)﴾ is conjoined to "the angels" by the conjunction of the specific to the general. And in one reading it is "Mikaa'eel" with a hamza and a yaa', and in another without a yaa'. ﴿Then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ He placed the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun "to them", to explain their condition.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 99:

﴿And We have certainly sent down to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿clear signs﴾, i.e., evident ones, [this being] a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) in reply to Ibn Ṣūriyā's statement to the Prophet: "You have brought us nothing." ﴿And none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾, who disbelieved in them.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 2, verse 100:**

﴿Is it that every time they made a covenant﴾ with God, ﴿a covenant﴾ concerning belief in the Prophet if he goes out, or concerning the Prophet's promise that they would not help the polytheists against him, ﴿a group of them threw it away﴾ (cast it aside) ﴿by breaking it.﴾ The answer to *kullamā* (كُلَّما, "every time," a temporal particle) is the implied clause, and the place of this clause is that of an interrogation expressing denial (*istifhām inkārī*). ﴿Rather﴾ (*bal*, here marking a transition to a new point), ﴿most of them do not believe.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 101:

﴿And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah﴾ [Muhammad (ﷺ)], ﴿confirming what was with them, a party of those who had been given the Book threw away the Book of Allah﴾ [i.e., the Torah] ﴿behind their backs﴾ [i.e., they did not act upon what was in it, including belief in the Messenger and others] ﴿as if they did not know﴾ [what was in it, that he is a true Prophet, or that it is the Book of Allah].

﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿نَبَذَ﴾ (they cast aside): ﴿مَا تَتْلُو﴾, i.e. what the devils recited (تَلَتْ), ﴿الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَىٰ﴾ during the reign (عَهْد) of ﴿مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ﴾, of sorcery (مِن السِّحْر). They had buried it beneath his throne (كُرْسِيّه) when his kingship was taken from him; or they used to eavesdrop (تَسْتَرِق السَّمْع), add lies to what they overheard, and convey it to the soothsayers (الكَهَنَة), who wrote it down. This spread and became widely known that the jinn knew the unseen. So Sulayman gathered the books and buried them. When he died, the devils showed the people where they were, and the people dug them up and found sorcery in them. They said: "Surely it was by this that Sulayman ruled you, so learn it," and they abandoned the books of their prophets. God Most High said, to absolve Sulayman and to refute the Jews in their claim, "Look at Muhammad mentioning Sulayman among the prophets, when he was merely a sorcerer": ﴿وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ﴾, i.e. he did not practise sorcery, for that would be disbelief (كَفَرَ). ﴿وَلَٰكِنَّ﴾ (read with both shaddah and without it) ﴿الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ﴾: this clause is a circumstantial clause (حال) from the pronoun in ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾. ﴿وَ﴾ they taught them ﴿مَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ﴾, i.e. what was inspired (أُلْهِماهُ) to them of sorcery; it is also read with the letter lām in the kasra form (الْمَلِكَيْنِ), the two who were ﴿بِبَابِلَ﴾, a town in the lower part of Iraq (سَواد العِراق). ﴿هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ﴾ is either a substitution (بَدَل) or an explanatory apposition (عَطْف بَيان) for the two angels. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "They were two magicians who used to teach sorcery." It was also said they were two angels sent down to teach it as a trial from God for the people. ﴿وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ﴾ (the ﴿مِنْ﴾ is extra) ﴿أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَا﴾ to him, as sincere counsel: ﴿إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ﴾, a affliction (بَلِيَّة) from God to the people, to test them through teaching it to them. Whoever learns it disbelieves, and whoever abandons it is a believer. ﴿فَلَا تَكْفُرْ﴾ by learning it. If he insists on learning, they teach him. ﴿فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ﴾, by causing each to hate the other. ﴿وَمَا هُمْ﴾, i.e. the sorcerers, ﴿بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ﴾, by the sorcery, ﴿مِنْ﴾ (extra) ﴿أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾, by His will. ﴿وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾, and that is sorcery. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾, the lām is a lām of oath, ﴿عَلِمُوا﴾, i.e. the Jews, ﴿لَمَنِ﴾ (the lām is an initial lām, linked to what precedes it, and مَنْ is a relative pronoun) ﴿اشْتَرَاهُ﴾, chose it or exchanged it for the Book of God, ﴿مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ﴾, a share (نَصِيب) in Paradise. ﴿وَلَبِئْسَ مَا﴾ (a thing) ﴿شَرَوْا﴾, sold ﴿بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾, i.e. the sellers, meaning their share of the Hereafter if they learned it, since it made the Fire obligatory for them. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the true reality of what they would come to of punishment, they would not have learned it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 103:

﴿And if only they had﴾ — i.e., the Jews — ﴿believed﴾ in the Prophet and the Qur'an, ﴿and feared Allah﴾ — (i.e., feared) the punishment of Allah by abandoning His disobediences, such as sorcery — and the response of "law" (law) is omitted: i.e., ﴿they would have been rewarded﴾, which is indicated by ﴿a reward﴾ (mathuba), meaning a recompense, which is the subject (mubtada'), and the lam in it is for oath (li-l-qasam), ﴿from Allah, is better﴾ — its predicate (khabar) — ﴿than what they have sold their souls for﴾. ﴿If only they knew﴾ that it is better, they would not have preferred what they preferred over it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 104:

﴿O you who have believed, do not say﴾ to the Prophet ﴿"Ra'ina"﴾. It is an imperative from al-mura'ah (observing, attending to someone's state; here, "pay attention to us"). They used to say this to him, and in the language of the Jews it was an insult derived from ru'ūnah (foolishness, stupidity). They were pleased with this and addressed the Prophet with it, so the believers were forbidden from it. ﴿But say﴾ instead ﴿"Unzurna"﴾, meaning "look upon us" (undhur ilayna). ﴿And listen﴾ to what you are commanded, listening with acceptance (sama' qabul). ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾, painful (mu'lim), and it is the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 105:

﴿Those who disbelieve among the People of the Book, and the polytheists, do not wish that any good be sent down to you from your Lord.﴾ The polytheists (al-mushrikin) from among the Arabs is conjoined (ʿutifa) to "the People of the Book," and "min" (from) is for explanation (li-l-bayan). ﴿That any good be sent down to you from﴾ the "min" here is extra (za'ida). ﴿Good﴾ means revelation (wahy), ﴿from your Lord﴾, out of envy towards you (hasadan lakum). ﴿And Allah singles out for His mercy﴾ His prophethood ﴿whom He wills. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 106:

When the disbelievers criticised abrogation (naskh) and said, "Muhammad commands his companions today to do one thing and forbids it tomorrow," the following was revealed: ﴿Whatever We abrogate of a verse﴾, where "whatever" (ma) is a conditional particle (sharṭiyya). ﴿Or cause it to be forgotten﴾ means: We postpone it, so We do not send down its ruling, and We lift its recitation; or We postpone it in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz). In another reading, without the hamza, from forgetting (al-nisyan), meaning: We cause you to forget it, that is, We erase it from your heart. The answer to the condition is ﴿We bring a better than it﴾, more beneficial for the servants in ease, or greater in reward, ﴿or its like﴾ in obligation and reward. ﴿Do you not know that Allah is over all things Competent?﴾ Among this is abrogation and substitution. The interrogative here is for affirmation (taqrir).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 107:

﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ He does what He wills. ﴿And you have not, besides Allah, any protector or any helper.﴾ That is, other than Him. ﴿Min﴾ is extra (zāʾida). ﴿Walī﴾ (protector) who will guard you; ﴿nor helper﴾ who will prevent His punishment from you should it come upon you. It was revealed when the people of Makkah asked Him to widen it (Makkah) and to make al-Safa into gold.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 108:

﴿Am﴾ (rather/or) ﴿do you wish to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked﴾ before? That is, his people asked him, ﴿before﴾ this, by saying: "Show us Allah openly," and other such things. ﴿And whoever exchanges disbelief for faith﴾ — that is, takes it in place of faith, by abandoning reflection on the signs and demanding other signs instead — ﴿has indeed strayed from the right way.﴾ The Arabic word al-sawa' (the middle, the balanced) in origin means the middle, and the right path is the true path.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 109:

﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after you have believed, out of envy from their own selves, after the truth has become clear to them﴾ — "law" here is a verbal particle (maṣdariyyah), ﴿they wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after you have believed, out of envy﴾ — ḥasadan is an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), being ﴿from their own selves﴾, meaning their wicked selves moved them to it ﴿after the truth had become clear to them﴾ in the Torah, concerning the matter of the Prophet ﴿So pardon﴾ them, meaning leave them alone ﴿and overlook﴾ — turn away, and do not repay them ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾ concerning them, that is, through fighting ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾.

﴿And establish prayer and give zakat. And whatever good you send forward for yourselves﴾ — obedience, such as ṣilah (keeping ties of kinship) and charity — ﴿you will find it﴾, i.e., its reward, ﴿with Allah. Indeed Allah, of what you do, is Seeing﴾, so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 111:

﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians.﴾ Hud is the plural of ha'id (Jew), [i.e., a Jew]. ﴿Or Christians.﴾ It was said that this was said by the Jews of Madinah and the Christians of Najran when they debated in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ. That is, the Jews said: None will enter it except the Jews, and the Christians said: None will enter it except the Christians. ﴿That﴾ statement ﴿is their wishful thinking.﴾ Their vain desires. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Produce your proof﴾, your argument for that, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 112:

﴿Yes!﴾ Others than them will enter Paradise, ﴿whoever submits his face to Allah﴾, i.e., surrenders to His command. He specified the face because it is the noblest of the limbs, so the rest is more deserving [of this submission]. ﴿And he is a doer of good﴾, a monotheist. ﴿For him is his reward with his Lord﴾, i.e., the reward of his deed, which is Paradise. ﴿No fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 113:

﴿And the Jews say: "The Christians are not upon anything,"﴾ [anything of worth], and they disbelieved in ʿIsa (Jesus). ﴿And the Christians say: "The Jews are not upon anything,"﴾ [anything of worth], and they disbelieved in Musa (Moses). ﴿And they [i.e., the two groups]﴾ ﴿recite the Book﴾ [that was revealed to them]; in the Jews' Book there is confirmation of ʿIsa, and in the Christians' Book there is confirmation of Musa. The clause is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). ﴿Likewise﴾ [as these said], ﴿those who have no knowledge said﴾ [i.e., the polytheists among the Arabs and others] ﴿the like of their saying﴾ [an explanation of the meaning of "likewise": that is, they said to every adherent of a religion, "You are not upon anything."] ﴿So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾ [regarding the matter of religion], so the righteous one (al-muḥiqq) will enter Paradise and the falsifier (al-mubṭil) the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 114:

﴿And who is more unjust﴾ meaning: none is more unjust ﴿than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein﴾ by prayer and glorification ﴿and strives for their ruin﴾ by demolishing them or by closing them down. It was revealed as a report concerning the Romans who ruined the House of the Holy (Bayt al-Maqdis), or concerning the polytheists when they barred the Prophet ﷺ from the House in the year of al-Hudaybiyah. ﴿It was not for them to enter them except in fear﴾: this is a report carrying the meaning of a command, i.e., frighten them with jihad, so that none enters them while secure. ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾: humiliation through killing, captivity and the jizyah (poll tax). ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾: it is the Fire.

Revealed when the Jews criticized the abrogation of the qibla (the direction of prayer), or the performance of voluntary prayer on a mount while traveling: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; so wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾. That is, the whole earth, because they are its two directions. ﴿Wherever you turn﴾ your faces in prayer, by His command, ﴿there is the Face of Allah﴾, that is, His qibla which He has approved. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing﴾, whose bounty encompasses everything, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of the arrangement of His creation.

And they say, with and without the conjunction [*wa*], "The Jews and the Christians, and whoever claimed that the angels are daughters of Allah, [say]: Allah has taken a son." Allah the Exalted said, "Glory be to Him" (*subhanahu*), declaring Him exempt from that (*tanzih*, declaring Allah free of imperfection). "Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth," in ownership, creation and servitude. Ownership is incompatible with begetting. He expressed it with *mā* (what) by way of *taghlib* (giving precedence to one form over another) for what does not reason. "All are devoutly obedient to Him" (*qānitūn*), each in what is willed of it. In it there is *taghlib* of the rational beings.

Badi' al-samawat wal-ard (the Originator of the heavens and the earth): their Creator, not upon any prior pattern. Wa-idha qada amran (And when He decrees a matter): i.e., wills it. Fa-innama yaqulu lahu kun fa-yakun (then He only says to it, "Be," and it is): i.e., so it comes into being. And in one recitation it is read with a fatha (fa-yakunu), as a response to the imperative (the ending "kun" is read as the subjunctive answer to the command).

And those who do not know say: "Why does Allah not speak to us, or a sign not come to us?" — that is, the Meccan disbelievers said to the Prophet (ﷺ). "Why does not" means "why not" (hallā). "Allah speak to us" — [declaring] that you are His messenger. "Or a sign come to us" — of the kind we have proposed as proof of your truthfulness. "Likewise" — as these people have said — "said those who came before them" — of the disbelieving nations of past times to their prophets — "a saying like their saying" — of obstinacy and demanding signs. "Their hearts have become alike" — in disbelief and stubbornness. In this there is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ). "We have indeed made the signs clear for a people who are certain" — who know that they are signs and therefore believe. So proposing a sign alongside them is obstinacy.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Tafsir of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 2, verse 119:

﴿Indeed, We have sent you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿with the truth﴾, meaning with the guidance, ﴿as a bringer of good news﴾ to whoever responds to it with Paradise, ﴿and a warner﴾ to whoever does not respond to it with the Fire. ﴿And you will not be questioned about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning the Fire, that is, the disbelievers: why have they not believed? ﴿Your duty is only to convey.﴾ And in one reading, *tusʼal* is read with a jazm (jussive), as a prohibition (nahy), i.e., "do not be questioned."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 120:

﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion﴾ (dinahum, i.e., their religion) ﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah﴾ (i.e., Islam) ﴿is the guidance﴾, and whatever else is other than it is misguidance. ﴿And if﴾ (the lam here is the lam of oath) ﴿you follow their desires﴾ which they call you to, supposing it hypothetically, ﴿after the knowledge that has come to you﴾ (i.e., the revelation from Allah) ﴿you will have no protector from Allah﴾ who would guard you, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who would prevent Him from you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 121:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ is the subject (mubtada'). ﴿recite it as it should be recited﴾, i.e., they read it as it was revealed. The clause is a circumstantial clause (hal). The word ḥaqq (truly, as it should be) is in the accusative as an absolute object (maṣdar), and the predicate follows. ﴿They believe in it﴾. It was revealed concerning a group who came from Abyssinia (al-Ḥabashah) and embraced Islam. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it﴾, i.e., in the Book that was given, by distorting it. ﴿Those are the losers﴾, because of their destiny to the Fire, which is everlasting for them.
﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and that I preferred you over the worlds﴾. A similar statement has already preceded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 123:

﴿And fear﴾ (ittaqu) fear ﴿a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all﴾ (la tajzi nafs 'an nafs) it will not suffice ﴿therein in anything, nor will ransom be accepted from it﴾ (wa la yuqbalu minha 'adl) compensation, ﴿nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped﴾ (wa la hum yunsaruna) they will be prevented from the punishment of Allah.
