﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when﴾ ﴿He tested﴾, that is, examined, ﴿Ibrahim﴾. In another reading it is Ibraham. ﴿His Lord with words﴾, meaning with commands and prohibitions that He imposed on him. It is said that these are the rites of the Hajj (pilgrimage). It is also said they are rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, using the siwak (tooth-stick), trimming the moustache, parting the hair, clipping the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, and istinja' (cleansing after relieving oneself). It would have been better for the discussion of being tested with the words to stop at the commands and prohibitions of the religion, because the Noble Qur'an did not specify the words with which God tested Ibrahim. The scholars' disagreement arises from determining these words. ﴿So he fulfilled them﴾, meaning he performed them completely. ﴿He said﴾, may He be exalted, to him: ﴿Indeed, I am making you an imam (leader) for the people﴾, meaning a model in religion. ﴿He said: "And from my offspring"﴾, meaning my children, ﴿make imams.﴾ ﴿He said: "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers"﴾, meaning the disbelievers among them, with respect to leadership. This indicates that it reaches those who are not wrongdoers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 125:

﴿And when We made the House[, i.e., the Ka'bah,] a place of return for the people﴾ [meaning a place to which they return] from every direction, ﴿and a sanctuary﴾ [a place of safety for them] from injustice and raids that occur elsewhere; a man would meet the killer of his father within it and would not molest him. ﴿And take﴾ O people (and in another reading, with the vowel of fatha on the kha', as a statement of fact) ﴿the station of Abraham﴾ [that is, the stone on which he stood during the building of the House] ﴿as a place of prayer﴾ [a place of prayer, by praying behind it the two rak'ahs of the circumambulation]. ﴿And We charged Abraham and Ishmael﴾ [We commanded them both] ﴿that﴾ [i.e., to] ﴿purify My House﴾ [from idols] ﴿for those who circumambulate it, and those who stay there﴾ [those who reside in it], ﴿and those who bow and prostrate﴾ [plural of rāki' and sājid, those who pray].

﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this"﴾ [the place] ﴿a secure land﴾, meaning a land of security. God answered his supplication and made it a *haram* (sanctuary) in which no human blood may be shed, no one may be wronged, its game may not be hunted, and its grass may not be cut. ﴿And provide its people with fruits﴾. God did so by transporting al-Ta'if from al-Sham (Greater Syria) to it, for it had been barren, with neither crops nor water. ﴿Those of them who believe in God and the Last Day﴾ is a *badal* (substitute, in grammatical terms an appositive) for "its people," and He specified them for the supplication in agreement with His saying, ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾. ﴿He said﴾, may He be exalted, ﴿And [I will provide for] those who disbelieve, I will grant them enjoyment﴾, read with *tashdid* (doubling of the letter) and with *takhfif* (lightening), ﴿for a little﴾ in this world, with provision, ﴿for the duration of their lives. Then I will compel them﴾, that is, force them, in the Hereafter ﴿to the punishment of the Fire﴾, so that they will find no escape from it. ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, the place of return it is.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 127:

﴿And﴾ remember ﴿when Ibrahim (Abraham) was raising the foundations﴾ (al-qawa'id), meaning the bases or the walls, ﴿of the House﴾ which he was building. ("min al-bayt" is connected to "yarfa'" [raising].) ﴿And Isma'il (Ishmael)﴾ is conjoined to Ibrahim, ﴿[the two] saying﴾: ﴿"Our Lord, accept from us"﴾ our building; ﴿"Indeed You, You are the All-Hearing"﴾ of the speech, ﴿"the All-Knowing"﴾ of the deed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 128:

﴿Our Lord, and make us submissive to You﴾ (muslimayn, i.e., compliant, submitting) ﴿and from our descendants a community submissive to You﴾: make our offspring a community (jama'ah) ﴿submissive to You.﴾ Min (from) here is for partition (li-l-tab'id), and it was mentioned here because of the prior statement, ﴿My covenant does not include the wrongdoers﴾. ﴿And show us﴾ teach us ﴿our rites (manasikana)﴾ the laws of our worship, or our hajj. ﴿And turn to us in forgiveness; indeed You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ They asked Him for repentance, along with their being protected from sin, out of humility and to teach their descendants.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 129:

﴿Our Lord, and send among them⦗a messenger from among them⦘﴾, i.e., from the people of this House (ahl al-bayt), ﴿a messenger from among them⦗from themselves⦘﴾, and Allah has answered his supplication with Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿who recites to them Your verses⦗the Qur'an⦘﴾, ﴿and teaches them the Book⦗the Qur'an⦘﴾ and ﴿the wisdom⦗i.e., what it contains of rulings⦘﴾, ﴿and purifies them⦗cleanses them from polytheism⦘﴾. ﴿Indeed You, You are the Mighty⦗the Overpowering⦘﴾, ﴿the Wise⦗in His creation⦘﴾.

﴿And who⦆ (i.e., none) ﴿would turn away from the creed (millah) of Ibrahim (Abraham)﴾ so as to abandon it, ﴿except one who makes a fool of himself﴾, being ignorant that he is a creation of God, whom it is obligatory upon him to worship, or who treats it lightly and debases it. ﴿And We certainly chose him﴾, We selected him ﴿in this world﴾ with prophethood and friendship (khullah, intimate closeness with God). ﴿And indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous﴾, those who have the lofty ranks.
And remember ﴿when his Lord said to him: "Submit"﴾, i.e., "Surrender to God and devote your religion sincerely to Him." ﴿He said: "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds."﴾

﴿And enjoined﴾, and in another reading (qira'ah) "advised" (awsa), ﴿by it﴾, meaning by the religion (millah), ﴿Ibrahim to his sons, and Ya'qub﴾, to his sons, saying: ﴿"O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you the religion﴾, the religion of Islam, ﴿so do not die except while you are Muslims."﴾ He forbade abandoning Islam and commanded them to remain steadfast upon it until death overtakes them.

When the Jews said to the Prophet, "Do you not know that Ya'qub (Jacob), on the day he died, enjoined his sons with Judaism?", the verse was revealed: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub?﴾ — present (ḥuḍūran) — ﴿when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?"﴾ — after my death. ﴿They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are submitting."﴾ Isma'il is counted among the fathers by way of taghlib (the dominance of one term over another), and also because the paternal uncle holds the status of a father (wa-li-anna al-'amm bi-manzilat al-ab). The phrase ﴿One God﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "your God." And ﴿Or⦅am⦆﴾ here carries the meaning of the interrogative hamza of denial (hamzat al-inkar), i.e., "You were not present at his death, so how can you attribute to him what is not befitting for him?"

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 2, verse 134:

﴿That﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and the reference is to Ibrahim, Ya'qub and their descendants; it is feminine because its predicate is feminine. ﴿a community that has passed away﴾, i.e., gone before. ﴿For them is what they earned﴾ from deeds, meaning its recompense. (This is a resumptive clause, isti'naf.) ﴿And for you is what you earned﴾, the address being to the Jews. ﴿And you will not be questioned about what they used to do﴾, just as they will not be questioned about your deeds. The sentence is an emphasis (ta'kid) of what precedes it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 135:

﴿And they say: "Be Jews or Christians, and you will be guided."﴾ "Or" is for distribution (tafsil). The speaker of the first is the Jews of Madinah, and the second the Christians of Najran. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Rather⁠—⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ we follow the religion of Ibrahim, ḥanīfan﴾ (ḥanīf, meaning upright and turning away from all religions toward the upright religion), being a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of Ibrahim, ﴿inclining away from all the religions to the upright religion. And he was not of the polytheists﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 136:

﴿Say﴾ is an address to the believers: ﴿We believe in God and in what has been sent down to us﴾ of the Qur'an, ﴿and in what was sent down to Ibrahim﴾ of the ten scrolls (suhuf), ﴿and Isma'il and Ishaq and Ya'qub and the Asbat﴾, his descendants. He (al-Mahalli or al-Suyuti) explained the Asbat as being the sons of Ya'qub. However, there is a consensus of the scholars (ittifaq al-'ulama') that prophethood does not apply to the ten brothers of Yusuf, other than Binyamin, because of their committing the wicked deeds which do not befit the station of prophethood. What is meant by the Asbat is the offspring of the brothers of Yusuf. ﴿And in what was given to Musa﴾ of the Torah, ﴿and Isa﴾ of the Gospel, ﴿and in what was given to the prophets from their Lord﴾ of the books and the signs. ﴿We make no distinction between any one of them﴾, so that we believe in some and disbelieve in others as the Jews and the Christians do. ﴿And to Him we are Muslims﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 137:

﴿Then if they believe in the like of that which you believe﴾, i.e., the Jews and the Christians, ﴿in the like﴾ (the particle "mithl" here is extra), ﴿of that which you believe, then they are [rightly] guided. But if they turn away﴾ from belief in it, ﴿then they are only in dissension﴾, opposition, ﴿against you﴾. ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them﴾, O Muhammad, [against] their dissension. ﴿And He is the Hearing﴾ of their statements, ﴿the Knowing﴾ of their conditions. He has indeed sufficed you against them by killing the Qurayzah, expelling the Nadir, and imposing the jizyah (poll tax) upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 138:

﴿The dye of Allah﴾ is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing "We have believed" (āmannā), and its accusative case is governed by a implied verb, meaning: "Allah has dyed us." What is meant by it is His religion upon which He created mankind, because its effect appears on its adherent like dye in cloth. ﴿And who﴾, meaning, no one, ﴿is better in dye than Allah﴾ is a specification (tamyīz). ﴿And we are worshippers of Him﴾. The Jews said to the Muslims: "We are the People of the Book, the first, and our qibla is older, and the prophets were not from the Arabs. If Muhammad (ﷺ) were a prophet, he would have been from us." So this verse was revealed.

﴿Say﴾ (to them): ﴿Do you dispute with us concerning Allah﴾, that is, argue with us, ﴿that He chose a Prophet from among the Arabs?﴾ ﴿And He is our Lord and your Lord﴾, so He has the right to choose whom He wills. "For us are our deeds," ﴿by which We will recompense﴾, "and for you are your deeds," ﴿by which you will be recompensed﴾. So it is not far-fetched that among our deeds there is that which merits honour, "and We are sincerely devoted to Him," ﴿in religion and in action, not you﴾, so we are more worthy of being chosen. The hamza (the interrogative particle, here a-) is for denial (inkar), and the three clauses (jumal) are circumstantial clauses (ahwal, sing. hal).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 140:

﴿Am﴾ (rather, or: "Or"), [they] ﴿say﴾ (read with the taa' and with the yaa'): ﴿Indeed Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes were Jews or Christians.﴾ Say [to them]: ﴿Are you more knowing, or is God?﴾ That is, God is more knowing. Abraham had already disassociated himself from both of them by His words: ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian﴾, and those mentioned with him are followers of him (tabaʿ, meaning followers or subordinates). ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals﴾ (hid from the people) ﴿a testimony he has from God﴾ (existing with him from God). That is, no one is more unjust than him, and they are the Jews, who concealed God's testimony in the Torah concerning Abraham's being a ḥanīf (upright monotheist, ḥanīfiyyah). ﴿And God is not unaware of what you do﴾: a warning to them.
﴿That was a community that has passed away. For them is what they earned, and for you is what you have earned, and you will not be questioned about what they used to do.﴾ Its like has preceded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 142:

﴿The foolish among the people will say﴾ the ignorant (al-sufaha'), and the use of "sa" (sa-, "will"), which indicates the future, is a foretelling of the unseen. ﴿Among the people﴾ the Jews and the polytheists. ﴿"What has turned them away﴾ i.e., what has turned the Prophet ﷺ and the believers ﴿from their qiblah, which they used to face﴾ in prayer, ﴿which is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)?﴾ ﴿Say: To God belong the east and the west﴾ i.e., all directions. So He commands facing whichever direction He wills, without objection to Him. ﴿He guides whom He wills﴾ to His guidance ﴿to a straight path﴾ a way, ﴿the religion of Islam.﴾ That is, among them are you (the Muslims). This is indicated by this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 143:

﴿And thus﴾ as We guided you to it, ﴿We have made you﴾ O community of Muhammad ﴿a community of the middle way﴾, meaning the best and most just, ﴿so that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, that their messengers conveyed to them, ﴿and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ that he conveyed to you. ﴿And We did not make﴾ We did not appoint ﴿the qiblah﴾ for you now, the direction ﴿which you used to face﴾ at first, which was the Ka'bah. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray facing it, but when he migrated, he was commanded to face Bayt al-Maqdis, to win over the Jews, so he prayed facing it for sixteen or seventeen months, then it was changed. ﴿Except that We might know﴾ with the knowledge of manifest observation ﴿who follows the Messenger﴾ by believing him ﴿from who turns back on his heels﴾, that is, who returns to disbelief, doubting the religion and supposing that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in confusion about his affair. A group apostatised on account of this. ﴿And indeed it﴾ — the word ﴿وإنْ﴾ here is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its noun is omitted, meaning: and indeed it — ﴿was﴾ that is, the turning towards it ﴿a great matter﴾, burdensome upon the people, ﴿except for those whom Allah guided﴾ among them. ﴿And Allah would not let your faith be lost﴾, meaning your prayers towards Bayt al-Maqdis, but rather He will reward you for them, because the occasion of its revelation was the question about those who died before the change. ﴿Indeed Allah is, toward the people﴾ the believers, ﴿Kind, Merciful﴾ in not losing their deeds. Ra'fah is an intensity of mercy, and it was placed first for the sake of the verse-ending (fasilah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 144:

﴿Qad﴾ (indeed) is for emphasis (tahqiq). ﴿We see﴾ the turning (taṣarruf) of ﴿your face﴾ toward ﴿the sky﴾ (jiha al-sama'), eagerly looking out for revelation and longing for the command to face the Ka'bah. He liked this, because it was the qiblah of Ibrahim, and because it was more likely to draw the Arabs to Islam. ﴿So We shall surely turn you﴾ (nuhawwilannaka), we shall change you, ﴿to a qiblah that you will be pleased with﴾ (turduha), that you love. ﴿So turn your face﴾ (fa-walli wajhaka), face (istaqbil) in prayer, ﴿toward the sacred mosque﴾ (shatra al-masjid al-haram), i.e., toward (nahw) the Ka'bah. ﴿Wherever you are﴾ is an address to the community (ummah), ﴿turn your faces﴾ in prayer ﴿toward it﴾ (shatrahu). ﴿Indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it﴾, i.e., the turning toward the Ka'bah, ﴿is the truth﴾ (al-haqq), the established (al-thabit) ﴿from their Lord﴾, because of what is in their books concerning the description (na't) of the Prophet ﷺ, that he would turn toward it. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what they do﴾: read with the ta' (you), O believers, regarding compliance with His command; and with the ya' (they), i.e., the Jews, regarding their denial of the matter of the qiblah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 145:

﴿And if﴾ the lam is the lam of oath (al-lam al-qasam) ﴿you were to bring those who were given the Book every sign﴾ as evidence of your truthfulness regarding the matter of the qibla, ﴿they would not follow﴾ your qibla, meaning they do not follow it, out of obstinacy ﴿your qibla﴾, ﴿and you are not one who follows their qibla﴾, a severing of his hope for their Islam and their hope for his return to it ﴿and some of them are not followers of the qibla of others﴾, meaning the Jews do not follow the qibla of the Christians and vice versa ﴿And if you were to follow their desires﴾ which they call you to ﴿after the knowledge that has come to you﴾, the revelation ﴿indeed you would then﴾, if you were to follow them hypothetically, ﴿be among the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 146:

﴿Those whom We have given the Book know him﴾ i.e., Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿as they know their own sons﴾ by his description in their books. Ibn Salam said: "I recognised him when I saw him just as I recognise my son, and my recognition of Muhammad is even stronger." ﴿And indeed a party of them conceal the truth﴾ his description, ﴿while they know﴾ that this is what you (ﷺ) are upon.

The truth (is) from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt (al-mumtarin), i.e., those who are skeptical about it. "Among those who doubt" means "of this kind," and this is more emphatic than saying "do not doubt."

For every nation there is a direction (qibla) toward which it turns [وِجْهَة], ﴿he turns toward it﴾ in his prayer; and in another reading, "mawlāhā" (the one who directs them, i.e., God) is read instead. ﴿So race to good deeds﴾: hasten to acts of obedience and to their acceptance. ﴿Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together﴾: He will gather you on the Day of Resurrection and recompense you for your deeds. ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 149:

﴿And from wherever you go forth﴾ for a journey, ﴿turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾ [i.e., its direction, the Ka'bah], ﴿and indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾ — with the ta' and the ya' (as recitation variants, i.e., "you do" and "they do"), the same as was mentioned before. He repeated it to clarify that the ruling for travel and for other circumstances is the same.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 150:

﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾ He repeated it for emphasis. ﴿So that people will have no argument against you﴾ — the Jews or the polytheists — ﴿except those of them who do wrong﴾; i.e., a dispute concerning the turning toward other than it, so that their disputing with you is eliminated, from the saying of the Jews, "He denies our religion and follows our qibla," and the saying of the polytheists, "He claims the creed of Ibrahim and opposes his qibla." ﴿Except those of them who do wrong﴾ through obstinacy, for they say, "He turned toward it only out of inclination to the religion of his fathers." The exception is connected, and the meaning is: no one will have an argument against you except the arguments of these people. ﴿So do not fear them﴾ — do not fear their disputing about the turning toward it — ﴿but fear Me﴾ by carrying out My command. ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you﴾ is conjoined to "so that people will have no argument," by guiding you to the landmarks of your religion. ﴿And that you may be guided﴾ to the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 151:

﴿كَما أرْسَلْنا﴾ (as We sent) is connected to ﴿أَتَمّ﴾ (perfect), meaning: the completion [of My favour upon you is] like the completion [of it] by Our sending ﴿فِيكُمْ رَسُولًا مِنكُمْ﴾ (among you a messenger from among you), namely Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿يَتْلُو عَلَيْكُمْ آياتنا﴾ (reciting to you Our verses), i.e. the Qur'an, ﴿ويُزَكِّيكُمْ﴾ (and purifying you), i.e. cleansing you from shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿ويُعَلِّمكُمْ الكِتاب﴾ (and teaching you the Book), i.e. the Qur'an, ﴿والحِكْمَة﴾ (and wisdom), i.e. the rulings contained in it, ﴿ويعلمكم ما لم تكونو تعلمون﴾ (and teaching you what you did not know).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 152:

﴿So remember Me﴾ with the prayer, glorification and the like, ﴿I will remember you﴾. It was said its meaning is: I will reward you. And in a hadith, from Allah: "Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than his gathering." ﴿And give thanks to Me﴾ for My blessings by obedience, ﴿and do not deny Me﴾ by disobedience.

O you who believe, seek help through patience (against the Hereafter) and prayer (al-salah). Patience is [to be exercised] in obedience and in affliction. He singled out prayer for mention because of its frequency and greatness. Indeed, Allah is with those who are patient, [giving them] help.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 154:

﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah﴾ they are ﴿dead. Rather﴾ they are ﴿alive﴾, their souls being in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, according to a hadith to that effect, ﴿but you do not perceive﴾, you do not know what they are in.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 155:

﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear﴾ from the enemy, ﴿and hunger﴾, meaning famine, ﴿and a loss of wealth﴾ through destruction, ﴿and lives﴾ through killing, death and illness, ﴿and fruits﴾ through the loss of crops, meaning: We will surely test you, so We will see whether you will be patient or not. ﴿And give good news to the patient﴾ in their trial, with Paradise.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 156:**

They are ﴿those who, when a calamity afflicts them﴾, a trial, ﴿say: "Indeed we belong to Allah"﴾, as His possession and slaves, He does with us what He wills, ﴿and indeed to Him we will return﴾ in the Hereafter, where He will recompense us. And in the hadith: (Whoever says "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" at the time of a calamity, Allah will reward him for it and will give him something better in its place). And in it, that the lamp of the Prophet (ﷺ) went out, and he said "Inna lillah wa inna ilayhi raji'un", and ʿĀ'ishah said: "It is only a lamp!" He said: (Everything that harms the believer is a calamity). Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Marasil.
﴿They are the ones upon whom are blessings﴾ (meaning) forgiveness "from their Lord and mercy" (meaning) favour, "and those are the ones who are guided" to the right course.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 158:

﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah﴾ are two mountains in Makkah. ﴿Among the symbols of Allah﴾ means the markers of His religion; it is the plural of sha'irah. ﴿So whoever performs Hajj to the House or performs 'Umrah﴾ means whoever enters into the state of Hajj or 'Umrah (talabbasa bi-l-hajj aw al-'umrah), and both originally mean intention and visitation. ﴿there is no blame upon him﴾ meaning no sin upon him ﴿in going back and forth between them﴾; in this, the ta' in the original (yatatawwaf) is assimilated into the ta' (tatah) [i.e., the form is yattawwaf], by going back and forth between them seven times. It was revealed when the Muslims disliked this, because the people of the Jahiliyyah used to circumambulate them while there were two idols upon them that they would touch. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that sa'y is not obligatory, due to what the removal of sin implies of optionality. Al-Shafi'i and others said it is a pillar (rukn). The Prophet ﷺ clarified its obligation by saying: (Indeed, Allah has prescribed for you the sa'y), narrated by al-Bayhaqi and others, and he said: (Begin with what Allah began with), meaning al-Safa, narrated by Muslim. ﴿And whoever volunteers good﴾; in another reading it is read with a yā' prefix and the ṭā' shaddah, in the jussive, and in it the ta' is assimilated into it, ﴿good﴾ meaning with good, i.e., he does what is not obligatory upon him of circumambulation or other acts. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Grateful﴾ for his deed, by rewarding him for it, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 159:

It was revealed concerning the Jews: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal﴾ the people ﴿what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance﴾ such as the verse of stoning (al-rajm) and the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿after We have made it clear for the people in the Scripture﴾ the Torah, ﴿those are cursed by Allah﴾ He removes them far from His mercy, ﴿and cursed by those who curse﴾ the angels and the believers, or everything, by invoking a curse upon them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 2, verse 160:

﴿Except those who repent﴾ — they turn back from that — ﴿and make amends﴾ — their deeds — ﴿and make clear﴾ — what they concealed — ﴿those, I will accept their repentance﴾ — I will accept their repentance — ﴿and I am the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful﴾ — toward the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 161:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers﴾ — this is a circumstantial clause (hal). ﴿Upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together﴾ — i.e., they deserve that in this world and the Hereafter. And "mankind" (al-nas) — it is said it is general, and it is said it refers to the believers.

﴿Abiding therein﴾: that is, the curse and the Fire, which is indicated by the reference to them. ﴿Their punishment will not be lightened for them﴾ even for the blink of an eye, ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾, that is, they will not be given respite for repentance or for an excuse.

It was revealed when they said, "Describe your Lord to us": ﴿And your God﴾, the One deserving of worship from among you, ﴿is One God﴾, having no like in His essence or in His attributes. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾, He is ﴿the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾. And they asked for a sign confirming this, so it was revealed:

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ and what is in them of wonders, ﴿and the alternation of the night and the day﴾ by their going and coming, and their increase and decrease, ﴿and the ships﴾ the vessels ﴿that sail in the sea﴾ and do not sink, laden ﴿with what benefits people﴾ of trade and cargo, ﴿and what Allah sends down from the sky of water﴾ rain, ﴿by which He gives life to the earth﴾ with vegetation ﴿after its death﴾ its dryness, ﴿and scatters﴾ He disperses and spreads ﴿therein every creature﴾ by it, because they thrive on the fertility that comes from it, ﴿and the variation of the winds﴾ turning them to the south and the north, hot and cold, ﴿and the clouds﴾ the overcast sky ﴿subjected﴾ made subservient by the command of Allah, the Exalted, moving wherever Allah wills, ﴿between the sky and the earth﴾ without any support, ﴿are signs﴾ indicating His oneness, the Exalted, ﴿for a people who use reason﴾ who reflect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 165:

﴿And among the people are those who take, besides Allah, equals (andad)﴾ i.e., other than Him, ﴿idols﴾, ﴿whom they love with the love due to Allah﴾ through glorification and submission, ﴿as they love Allah﴾ i.e., as they love Him. ﴿But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah﴾ than their love for the equals, because they never turn away from Him in any state, whereas the disbelievers turn away from Him in times of severity to [other] than Allah. ﴿If only those who have wronged could see﴾ — O Muhammad, you would see — by taking equals, ﴿when they see the punishment﴾ — the verb may be read with the active or passive form — ﴿that all power belongs to Allah entirely﴾ — a circumstantial clause — ﴿and that Allah is severe in punishment﴾ — in another reading "tara" (you see), with the subject being the addressee. It is also said that the subject is "those who have wronged," in which case the verb means "know," and "that" and what follows it take the place of the two objects. The answer to "law" (if only) is omitted, and the meaning is: if they had known in the world the severity of Allah's punishment and that power belongs to Allah alone, at the time of their witnessing it, which is the Day of Resurrection, [they would not have] taken equals besides Him.

﴿When﴾ is a substitute for ﴿when﴾ before it: ﴿those who were followed disowned﴾ those who were followed, i.e., the leaders, ﴿those who followed﴾, i.e., they denied misguiding them. ﴿And﴾ [when] ﴿they saw the punishment, and their bonds were cut﴾ is conjoined to ﴿disowned﴾; ﴿with them﴾, from them, ﴿the ties﴾, the connections that had been between them in the world, of kinship and affection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 167:

﴿And those who followed said: "If only we had a return [to the world]"﴾ — a return to the worldly life, even if only as a wish — "and we would disown them" as an answer to the "if only" — ﴿so that we would disown them﴾, i.e., the ones who were followed, ﴿just as they have disowned us﴾ today. ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., just as He showed them the severity of His punishment, ﴿and some of them disowned others﴾, ﴿Allah will show them their deeds﴾, the evil ones, ﴿as regrets﴾, a state of remorse, ﴿upon them. And they will not be ones who come out of the Fire﴾ after having entered it.

It was revealed concerning those who forbade the sawa'ib (free-roaming camels) and the like: ﴿O mankind, eat of what is in the earth, lawful and good﴾. "Lawful" (halalan) is a circumstantial qualifier (hal). "Good" (tayyiban) is an emphasizing qualifier (sifa mu'akkida), meaning palatable. ﴿And do not follow the footsteps﴾ (khutuwat, meaning paths) ﴿of Satan﴾, i.e. his adornment (of evil). ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾, whose enmity is manifest.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 169:

﴿Indeed, he commands you only to evil﴾ (al-su') sin (al-ithm), ﴿and immorality﴾ (al-fahsha') what is ugly in the Sharia, ﴿and that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾ of prohibiting what He did not prohibit, and other than that.

When it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," [the disbelievers] say, "No, we will follow what we found our fathers upon." [Allah says:] Even if their fathers had no understanding of anything [of the matter of religion] and were not guided [to the truth]?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 171:

﴿And the likeness﴾ (i.e., the description) of ﴿those who disbelieve﴾ and of the one who calls them to guidance ﴿is like that of one who shouts﴾ (yunʿiq), i.e., vocalizes ﴿to that which hears nothing but a call and a cry﴾, i.e., a sound, and does not understand its meaning; that is, in hearing the admonition and not reflecting upon it, like the cattle that hear the voice of their shepherd and do not understand it. They are ﴿deaf, dumb, blind; so they do not understand﴾ the admonition.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 172:

﴿O you who have believed, eat from the good things (ḥalālāt) that We have provided for you, and be grateful to Allah, if it is Him that you worship.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 173:

﴿Indeed He has forbidden you carrion﴾, i.e., eating it, since the discussion concerns it, and likewise what follows it. Carrion is that which has not been slaughtered according to the Sharia (law). Attached to it by the Sunnah is what is cut off from a living animal. Excepted from it are fish and locusts. ﴿And blood﴾, i.e., that which is poured forth, as in Surah al-An'am. ﴿And the flesh of swine﴾: the flesh was singled out because it is the principal intended part, and the rest follows it. ﴿And that over which other than Allah has been invoked﴾, i.e., that which was slaughtered in the name of other than Allah. Al-ihlal (invocation) means raising the voice, and they used to raise their voices at slaughter for their idols. ﴿But whoever is compelled﴾, i.e., whom necessity drives to eat any of what has been mentioned, and so he eats it, ﴿without desiring [it] or transgressing﴾, i.e., rebelling against the Muslims, ﴿nor exceeding [the need]﴾, i.e., aggressing against them by highway robbery, ﴿then there is no sin upon him﴾ in eating it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward His allies, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward the people of His obedience, in that He has granted them latitude in this. The rebellious one and the aggressor are excluded, and every sinner in his journey is attached to them, such as a runaway slave and a tax collector who levies unlawful tolls. So it is not lawful for them to eat any of that as long as they do not repent. Al-Shafi'i held this view.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 174:

﴿Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book﴾, which includes the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they are the Jews, ﴿and sell it for a small price﴾ of the worldly life, taking in exchange for it some of their inferior people, so they do not make it manifest, out of fear of losing that [gain] from them. ﴿Those [people] eat not into their bellies except the Fire﴾, because it is their final destination. ﴿And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, out of anger toward them. ﴿Nor will He purify them﴾, that is, cleanse them from the defilement of sins. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾, painful, which is the Fire.

Those are the ones who purchased error in place of guidance, taking it as a substitute for it in the world, and punishment in place of forgiveness, which was prepared for them in the Hereafter had they not concealed [the truth]. ﴿So how patient they are for the Fire!﴾ That is, how intense is their endurance [of it]. This is an expression of wonder on the part of the believers at their committing that which necessitates it, without any concern; otherwise, what patience do they have?

That is (the state described above: their eating of the Fire and what follows), because (بِأَنَّ) of the fact that Allah sent down the Book with truth, related to "sent down" (نَزَّلَ). They differed about it, for they believed in part of it and disbelieved in part of it by concealing it. And indeed those who differed concerning the Book (in this way), namely the Jews, and it was said the polytheists concerning the Qur'an, when some of them said it is poetry, some said it is sorcery, and some said it is soothsaying, are in extreme opposition (shiqaq: opposition) far (ba'id: distant) from the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 177:

﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces﴾ in the prayer ﴿toward the east or the west﴾. It was revealed in refutation of the Jews and Christians, who claimed that this was righteousness. ﴿But righteousness is﴾, i.e., the one who has righteousness (*dhā al-birr*). It is also recited with a fatḥa on the bāʾ, as *al-bārr*, meaning "the one who is righteous." ﴿is he who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book﴾, i.e., the books, ﴿and the prophets, and gives wealth, despite [ʿalā, here meaning maʿa, "with"] love for it, to relatives ﴿kinsfolk﴾, meaning kinship, ﴿orphans, the needy, the wayfarer﴾, meaning the traveller, ﴿and those who ask﴾, meaning the petitioners, ﴿and for﴾, meaning the freeing of ﴿captives﴾, meaning those seeking manumission (*al-mukātabīn*) and prisoners of war, ﴿and establishes prayer and gives zakat﴾, meaning the obligatory zakat; what precedes it refers to voluntary charity. ﴿And those who fulfil their covenant when they make it﴾, with Allah or with people, ﴿and the patient﴾, *al-ṣābirīn* (والصّابِرِينَ), put in the accusative by way of praise (*naṣb ʿalā al-madḥ*), ﴿in misfortune﴾, meaning severe poverty, ﴿and hardship﴾, meaning illness, ﴿and in time of violence﴾, meaning the time of severe fighting in the way of Allah. ﴿Those are the ones who are true﴾ in their faith or in their claim to righteousness, ﴿and those are the righteous (*al-muttaqūn*)﴾ of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 178:

﴿O you who have believed, prescribed for you is⟩ it was made obligatory upon you ﴿retaliation (al-qisas)⟩ equality (al-mumathala) ﴿concerning the slain⟩ in description and in act. ﴿The free⟩ shall be killed ﴿for the free⟩ and he shall not be killed for the slave, ﴿and the slave for the slave, and the female for the female⟩. The Sunnah clarified that the male is killed for her, and that equality is taken into account in religion, so a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever, even if the Muslim is a slave and the disbeliever is free. ﴿But whoever is pardoned⟩ by the killers ﴿from⟩ the blood of ﴿his brother⟩, the slain, ﴿anything⟩, by leaving retaliation against him. The indefinite "anything" indicates that retaliation falls away by pardoning part of it, or by pardon from some of the heirs. Mentioning "his brother" is an inducement to pardon and an indication that killing does not sever the brotherhood of faith. "Whoever" is either a conditional or a relative subject, and the predicate is: ﴿then pursuing⟩, that is, the pardoner's act is a pursuit of the killer ﴿with kindness⟩, by demanding the blood-money from him without harshness. The ordering of "pursuing" after "pardon" indicates that the obligation is one of the two, and this is one of al-Shafi'i's two opinions. The second is that the obligation is retaliation, with the blood-money as a substitute for it. So if he pardons and does not specify anything, then there is nothing. ﴿And⟩ it is incumbent upon the killer ﴿to pay⟩ the blood-money ﴿to him⟩, that is, to the pardoner, who is the heir, ﴿with good conduct⟩, without delay or diminution. ﴿That⟩, the aforementioned ruling, namely the permissibility of retaliation and of pardoning it in exchange for blood-money, ﴿is a lightening⟩, an facilitation, ﴿from your Lord⟩ upon you, ﴿and a mercy⟩ upon you, in that He made it broad in this matter and did not make either of the two absolutely binding, as He made retaliation binding upon the Jews and blood-money binding upon the Christians. ﴿So whoever transgresses⟩, wrongs the killer by killing him ﴿after that⟩, that is, after the pardon, ﴿for him is a painful punishment⟩, painful in the Hereafter, by the Fire, or in this world, by being killed.

﴿And for you in retribution (al-qisas) there is life﴾, i.e., great survival. ﴿O you of understanding﴾, possessors of intellects, because when the killer knows that he will be killed, he refrains, thereby preserving his own life and the life of whoever wished to kill him, and so the law was prescribed. ﴿That you may be God-fearing﴾, avoiding killing for fear of retaliation (al-qawad).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 180:

﴿It is prescribed﴾ (kutiba), i.e., it is made obligatory, ﴿upon you, when death approaches any one of you﴾ (idha hadara ahadakum al-mawt), i.e., its signs, ﴿if he leaves behind wealth﴾ (in taraka khayran), i.e., property, ﴿that he make a bequest﴾ (al-wasiyya). It is in the nominative, governed by kutiba, and is connected to idha if it is adverbial (zarfiyya), and it indicates its response if it is conditional (shartiyya). The response of in is: fa-l-yuwsi (then let him make a bequest), ﴿to the parents and the nearest relatives, in accordance with what is fair﴾ (bil-ma'ruf), i.e., with justice, by not exceeding one-third and not favouring the wealthy, ﴿as a duty﴾ (haqqan), a verbal noun emphasising the content of the sentence before it, ﴿upon those who are mindful [of God]﴾ (al-muttaqin), i.e., of Allah. This ruling has been abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of inheritance and by the hadith: "There is no bequest to an heir," narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 2, verse 181:

﴿Then whoever alters it﴾ i.e., the bequest, by a witness or an executor (waṣī), ﴿after he has heard it﴾ i.e., known it, ﴿its sin is only upon those who alter it.﴾ i.e., the altered bequest; here the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾ of the words of the testator, ﴿Knowing﴾ of the act of the executor, and so He will recompense him for it.

﴿Then whoever fears injustice (janaf) from a testator (mūṣin), whether through error or deliberately (both readings, mukhaffafan and muthaqqalan, are recited)—meaning a deviation from the truth through error, or sin (ithm), namely by deliberately exceeding the one-third or favouring a wealthy heir, for example—and makes peace between them, between the testator and the beneficiary, by commanding justice, there is no sin upon him in that. Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

O you who believe! Fasting has been prescribed for you (kutiba, i.e. was made obligatory) as it was prescribed for those before you, from among the nations, so that you may become God-fearing (la'allakum tattaqun), i.e. (avoiding) sins, for it breaks the desire (al-shahwa) which is their source.

﴿Days numbered﴾ is in the accusative, governed either by "fasting" or by an implied "they should fast." ﴿Numbered﴾ means few, or fixed by a known count, and these days are Ramadan, as will come. He made them few to ease the burden on those under obligation. ﴿Whoever among you is﴾ at the time of its witnessing ﴿sick or on a journey﴾, meaning a traveler on a journey that permits shortening the prayer (qasr), and fasting exhausts him in either case, so he breaks his fast, ﴿then a number﴾, meaning he owes the number of days he broke, ﴿from other days﴾ which he fasts in its place. ﴿And for those who﴾ are not able ﴿to endure it﴾ because of old age or an illness from which recovery is not expected, ﴿there is a ransom﴾, which is ﴿feeding a poor person﴾, meaning an amount sufficient for what he eats on that day, namely one mudd (a measure) from the staple food of the region, for each day. In another reading (qira'ah), "ransom" is in construct with "feeding," where the second term explains the first (lil-bayan). It is also said that the ransom is not specified by a particular amount. In the early period of Islam they were given a choice between fasting and the ransom, and then this was abrogated (naskh) by the specification of fasting in His words: ﴿whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: except for the pregnant and the nursing woman when they break their fast out of fear for the child; for them the ransom remains in force without abrogation. ﴿Whoever volunteers good﴾, by exceeding the amount mentioned for the ransom, ﴿then it﴾, that is the voluntary act, ﴿is better for him. And that you fast﴾ is the subject, whose predicate is ﴿better for you﴾ than breaking the fast and paying the ransom, ﴿if you know﴾ that it is better for you, so do it.

That [i.e., these days]: ﴿the month of Ramadan, in which the Qur'an was revealed﴾ from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven, on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) within it. ﴿A guidance﴾, a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the Qur'an at revelation), guiding away from misguidance, ﴿for mankind, and clear proofs﴾, verses that are evident, ﴿of the guidance﴾, by which one is led to the truth regarding the rulings, ﴿and the Criterion﴾, and of the Criterion, by which truth is distinguished from falsehood. ﴿So whoever of you witnesses﴾, is present for, ﴿the month, let him fast it. And whoever is ill or on a journey, then [let him fast] a number of other days﴾. This was mentioned previously and repeated lest it be supposed that it had been abrogated (naskh, abrogation) by the generality of "whoever witnesses" (مَن شَهِدَ). ﴿God intends for you ease, and does not intend for you hardship﴾. For this reason He permitted you to break the fast during illness and travel, since that carries the same meaning of the ʿillah (underlying reason) for the command to fast. It is conjoined to it: ﴿and that you complete the period﴾, read with takhfif (lightened) and tashdid (emphasized) forms of the verb, ﴿the period﴾, i.e., the period of fasting in Ramadan, ﴿and that you glorify God﴾ at its completion, ﴿for having guided you﴾, shown you the landmarks of His religion, ﴿and perhaps you will be thankful﴾ to God for that.

A group asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "Is our Lord near, so that we may confide to Him, or far, so that we must call out to Him?" So it was revealed: ﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near﴾ to them by My knowledge, and He informed them of that. ﴿I answer the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾ by granting him what he asks. ﴿So let them respond to Me﴾ (i.e., to My call) ﴿by obedience﴾. ﴿And let them believe﴾ in Me, that is, let them persist in faith in Me, ﴿that they may be guided﴾, that is, that they may be rightly guided.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 187:

﴿It has been made lawful for you, on the night of the fast, to go in unto your wives (al-rafath)﴾ meaning (bi-ma'na) al-ifdaa' (intimate relations), ﴿to your wives﴾ by intercourse (bi-l-jima'). It was revealed as an abrogation (naskh) of what was in the early period of Islam, namely its prohibition, and the prohibition of eating and drinking after the night prayer (al-'isha'). ﴿They are a garment for you and you are a garment for them﴾, a metaphor (kinaya) for the embrace of each of them, or for the need each of them has for the other. ﴿Allah knew that you were betraying yourselves﴾ (takhununa), i.e. you were wronging yourselves, ﴿by intercourse on the night of the fast; this happened to Umar and others, and they apologized to the Prophet (ﷺ)﴾. ﴿So He turned to you in forgiveness﴾ before your repentance ﴿and pardoned you. So now﴾ since it has been made lawful for you, ﴿lie with them﴾ (bashiruhunna), i.e. have intercourse with them, ﴿and seek﴾ (ibtaghu), i.e. seek, ﴿what Allah has decreed for you﴾, i.e. what He has permitted of intercourse, or what He has destined of offspring. ﴿And eat and drink﴾ throughout the night ﴿until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread at dawn﴾, i.e. the true dawn. The explanation (bayan) of "the white thread" is the clarification, and the explanation of "the black thread" is omitted, i.e. "of the night", resembling what appears of whiteness and what extends with it of dimness, with two threads, white and black, in their extension. ﴿Then complete the fast﴾ from dawn ﴿until the night﴾, i.e. until its onset by the sun's setting. ﴿And do not lie with them﴾, i.e. your wives, ﴿while you are in devotional retreat (i'tikaf), remaining in the mosques﴾ (fi al-masajid). The phrase "in the mosques" is connected with "in devotional retreat"; this is a prohibition for one who would leave while in retreat, have intercourse with his wife, and then return. ﴿These﴾ aforementioned rulings are ﴿the limits of Allah﴾, which He set for His servants so that they would stop at them. ﴿So do not approach them﴾, which is more emphatic than "do not transgress them", the expression used in another verse. ﴿Thus﴾, as He has clarified for you what has been mentioned, ﴿Allah makes clear His signs to mankind that they may be God-fearing﴾, i.e. that they may avoid His prohibitions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 188:

﴿And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾, meaning: some of you devour the wealth of others ﴿unjustly﴾, that is, what is forbidden by the Law, such as theft and usurpation. ﴿And﴾ do not ﴿send it﴾, i.e., cast it, ﴿[as bribes] to the rulers﴾ — that is, [do not cast] its judgment, or the wealth, as a bribe ﴿so that you may consume a portion of the wealth of the people﴾ by litigation ﴿in sin﴾, being ﴿aware﴾ that you are ﴿wrongdoers﴾.

﴿They ask you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿about the crescents﴾, the plural of hilal (crescent moon), which do not appear fine at first, then grow until they become full of light, then return as they first appeared, and are not in one state the way the sun is. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿They are fixed times﴾, the plural of miqat (appointed time), ﴿for the people﴾, by which they know the times of their sowing, their trade, the counts of their women (i.e., their waiting periods), their fasting and their breaking of the fast. ﴿And the Hajj﴾ is coordinated with "the people", meaning that by them one knows its time, for if the moon remained in one state, that would not be known. ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter the houses from their backs﴾ while in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for pilgrimage), by making a breach in them through which you enter and exit while leaving the door. They used to do this and claimed it to be righteousness. ﴿But righteousness is﴾, i.e., the one who possesses righteousness, ﴿whoever fears God﴾ by abstaining from disobeying Him. ﴿And enter the houses through their doors﴾ in the state of ihram. ﴿And fear God that you may prosper﴾, that you may succeed.

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was prevented from the House in the year of al-Hudaybiyya, and he made a treaty with the disbelievers that he would return the following year and they would vacate Makkah for him for three days, and he prepared for the ʿUmrat al-Qadaʾ (the make-up ʿUmrah), and they feared that Quraysh would not keep the treaty and would fight them, and the Muslims disliked fighting them in the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), while in the state of ihram, and in the sacred month, the following was revealed: ﴿And fight in the way of God﴾, i.e., to raise His religion, ﴿those who fight you﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿but do not transgress﴾ against them by initiating the fighting, ﴿Indeed, God does not love the transgressors﴾, those who exceed the limit set for them. This is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of Baraʾah (al-Tawbah), or by His saying:

﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them﴾, i.e., find them, ﴿and expel them from where they expelled you﴾, i.e., from Makkah. This was done to them in the year of the Conquest. ﴿And fitnah﴾, i.e., shirk (polytheism) on their part, ﴿is worse﴾, i.e., greater, ﴿than killing﴾ them in the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) or in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for pilgrimage), which you regarded as grave. ﴿And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque﴾, i.e., within the Haram, ﴿until they fight you there. But if they fight you﴾ there, ﴿then kill them﴾ there. In another recitation, the three verbs in this passage are read without alif (the qira'ah of the reciters). ﴿Such is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾, namely the killing and the expulsion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 2, verse 192:

﴿But if they desist﴾ from disbelief and embrace Islam, ﴿then surely Allah is All-Forgiving﴾ toward them, ﴿All-Merciful﴾ to them.

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾, meaning shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah﴾, meaning worship is for Allah alone, and none is worshipped besides Him. ﴿But if they desist﴾ from shirk, then do not transgress against them. This indicates ﴿there is no hostility﴾, meaning no aggression by killing or otherwise, ﴿except against the wrongdoers﴾. Whoever desists is not a wrongdoer, so there is no hostility against him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 194:

﴿The sacred month﴾ (al-muharram) corresponds to ﴿the sacred month﴾, so whenever they fight you in it, then fight them in the like of it. This is a response to the Muslims' apprehension about that. ﴿And the sacred things﴾ is the plural of ḥurmah, that which must be respected; ﴿retaliation﴾ means that one retaliates in kind if they are violated. ﴿So whoever transgresses against you﴾ by fighting in the sacred precinct (al-ḥaram), or in the state of ihram, or in the sacred month, ﴿then transgress against him in like manner as he transgressed against you﴾. He called the response an "transgression" because of its resemblance to the act it answers, in form. ﴿And fear God﴾ in seeking victory and in refraining from transgression, ﴿and know that God is with those who fear Him﴾ by help and victory.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 195:

﴿And spend in the cause of Allah﴾ — (i.e.) in obedience to Him, by means of jihad and other than it. ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands﴾ — i.e., your own selves; the "bi" (with) is extra. ﴿into destruction﴾ — the ruin, by refraining from spending in jihad or abandoning it, for that strengthens the enemy against you. ﴿And do good﴾ — by spending and otherwise. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾ — i.e., He will reward them.

﴿وأَتِمُّوا الحَجّ والعُمْرَة لِلَّهِ﴾ (And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah): perform them with their rights (huquq). ﴿فَإنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ﴾ (But if you are prevented): you are hindered from completing them by an enemy. ﴿فَما اسْتَيْسَرَ﴾ (then what is feasible) means what is made easy. ﴿مِن الهَدْي﴾ (of the sacrificial animal, hady) for you, and it is a sheep. ﴿ولا تَحْلِقُوا رُءُوسكُمْ﴾ (And do not shave your heads) means do not exit the state of ihram (tahallul). ﴿حَتّى يَبْلُغ الهَدْي﴾ (until the sacrificial animal reaches) the one mentioned ﴿مَحِلّه﴾ (its place of sacrifice), where it is permissible to slaughter it, and that is the place of the ihsar according to al-Shafi'i (ash-Shafi'i). So one slaughters it there with the intention of exiting ihram, distributes it to its poor, and shaves, and by this the exit from ihram is achieved. ﴿فَمَن كانَ مِنكُمْ مَرِيضًا أوْ بِهِ أذًى مِن رَأْسه﴾ (So whoever among you is ill or has an injury of the head) such as lice or headache, so he shaves while in ihram, ﴿فَفِدْيَة﴾ (then there is a ransom) for him ﴿مِن صِيام﴾ (of fasting) three days, ﴿أوْ صَدَقَة﴾ (or charity) of three sa' of the staple food of the land, to six poor people, ﴿أوْ نُسُك﴾ (or a sacrifice), that is, slaughtering a sheep. Here "aw" (or) is for choice. Whoever shaves without an excuse is included with this, because he is more deserving of expiation (kaffarah). Likewise whoever enjoys (istamta'a) other than shaving, such as perfume, clothing, or oil, whether for an excuse or otherwise. ﴿فَإذا أمِنتُمْ﴾ (Then when you are secure) from the enemy, by its departure or its absence, ﴿فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ﴾ (then whoever benefits from) ﴿بِالعُمْرَةِ﴾ (the 'Umrah), that is, by reason of his having finished it, from the prohibitions of ihram, ﴿إلى الحَجّ﴾ (until the Hajj), that is, until entering ihram for it, by having entered ihram for 'Umrah in its months. ﴿فَما اسْتَيْسَرَ﴾ (then what is feasible) ﴿مِن الهَدْي﴾ (of the sacrificial animal) for him, which is a sheep that he slaughters after entering ihram for the Hajj, and the best time is the day of sacrifice (yawm an-nahr). ﴿فَمَن لَمْ يَجِد﴾ (But whoever does not find it), due to its unavailability or the unavailability of its price, ﴿فَصِيام﴾ (then fasting) means he must fast ﴿ثَلاثَة أيّام فِي الحَجّ﴾ (three days during the Hajj), that is, while in ihram for it. It is then obligatory that he enters ihram before the seventh of Dhu al-Hijjah, and the best is before the sixth, due to the disliked nature of fasting on the Day of 'Arafah, and it is not permissible to fast them on the days of tashriq according to the more correct of al-Shafi'i's two opinions. ﴿وسَبْعَة إذا رَجَعْتُمْ﴾ (and seven when you return) to your homeland, Makkah or otherwise. It is said: when you have finished the rites of the Hajj. There is here a shift (iltifat) from the third person (ghaybah). ﴿تِلْكَ عَشَرَة كامِلَة﴾ (That is ten complete) is a sentence emphasizing what precedes it. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ (That) ruling mentioned, of the obligation of the sacrificial animal or fasting, upon whoever benefits (from 'Umrah to Hajj), ﴿لِمَن لَمْ يَكُنْ أهْله حاضِرِي المَسْجِد الحَرام﴾ (is for those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque), meaning they are not within less than two stages (marhalatayn) from the Sacred Mosque according to al-Shafi'i. If they are, then there is no sacrifice or fasting upon him. If he enjoys, then it is obligatory upon him, and this is one of two opinions of al-Shafi'i; the second says no. "Ahl" (family) is a metonym for the self. Included with the one who performs tamattu' in what has been mentioned by the Sunnah is the qarin (one who combines), who is the one who enters ihram for 'Umrah and Hajj together, or who makes the Hajj enter upon the 'Umrah before the tawaf. ﴿واتَّقُوا اللَّه﴾ (And fear Allah) regarding what He commands you and forbids you. ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّه شَدِيد العِقاب﴾ (And know that Allah is severe in punishment) for whoever opposes Him.

﴿The Hajj﴾ its time ﴿is in well-known months﴾: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah, and it was said that the whole of Dhu al-Hijjah is included. ﴿Whoever imposes upon himself﴾ by entering the state of ihram for it, ﴿within them the Hajj﴾. ﴿There shall be no sexual intercourse﴾, meaning intercourse during it, ﴿nor transgression﴾, meaning sins, ﴿nor disputing﴾, meaning quarrelling, ﴿during the Hajj﴾. In another qira'a (a canonical recitation), the first two words are read with a fatha, �ином... Its sense is that the words "there shall be no" are a nahy (a prohibition). ﴿And whatever good you do﴾, such as giving charity, ﴿Allah knows it﴾, and will reward you for it. It was revealed concerning the people of Yemen, who used to perform the Hajj without provisions, so they became burdens upon the people. ﴿And take provisions﴾ that will suffice you for your journey, ﴿for the best provision is piety﴾, that by which one guards oneself against asking people and other things. ﴿And fear Me, O people of understanding﴾, meaning those of intellect.

﴿There is no blame upon you﴾ in ﴿seeking﴾ (tabtaghū), i.e. seeking ﴿bounty﴾ (faḍlan), meaning provision, ﴿from your Lord﴾ through trade during the Hajj. It was revealed in response to their dislike of that. ﴿Then when you pour forth﴾ (afaḍtum), i.e. you move on, ﴿from ʿArafāt﴾ after standing there, ﴿remember Allah﴾ after spending the night at Muzdalifah, with the talbiyah, the tahlil and supplication, ﴿at the Sacred Monument﴾ (al-mashʿar al-ḥarām), which is a mountain at the far end of Muzdalifah called Quzaḥ. In a ḥadīth it is related that he (ﷺ) stood there remembering Allah and supplicating until it became very bright; narrated by Muslim. ﴿And remember Him as He has guided you﴾ to the landmarks of His religion and the rites of His Hajj; the kāf here indicates causality (ta'līl). ﴿And indeed﴾ (wa-in, with the particle lightened/mukhaffafah), ﴿you were before it﴾, i.e. before His guidance, ﴿surely among the astray﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 199:

﴿Then depart﴾ O Quraysh, ﴿from where the people depart﴾, i.e., from ʿArafah, by standing there with them. They (Quraysh) used to stand at al-Muzdalifah, out of haughtiness toward standing together with them. And "thumma" (then) here indicates sequence in mention, ﴿and seek forgiveness from Allah﴾ for your sins. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward the believers, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 200:

﴿So when you have completed﴾ you have performed ﴿your rites﴾ the acts of worship of your Hajj, by having thrown the pebbles at the Jamrat al-'Aqabah, performed the circumambulation (tawaf), and settled in Mina; ﴿then remember God﴾ with takbir (saying Allahu akbar) and praise; ﴿as you remember your fathers﴾ as you used to remember them at the end of your Hajj, with boasting; ﴿or with a more intense remembrance﴾ than your remembrance of them. The word ashadd (more intense) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the object of the imperative udhkuru (remember), for if it were placed after it, it would be an attribute of it.

﴿Among people there is one who says: "Our Lord, give us"﴾ a share ﴿in this world﴾ and He gives him in it; ﴿but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ no portion (khalaq, meaning share).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 201:

﴿And among them is he who says: "Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good"﴾ meaning, a blessing, ﴿and in the Hereafter that which is good﴾ which is Paradise, ﴿and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ by not entering it. And this is an explanation of what the polytheists were upon and of the state of the believers, and the purpose of it is to urge seeking the good of both abodes, as He promised the reward for it with His saying:

﴿For them there is a share﴾ of reward "from" (min) ﴿what they earned﴾ by their deeds in the Hajj (pilgrimage) and the supplication (du'a), ﴿and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, He reckons all creation in the span of half a day of the days of this world, according to a hadith to that effect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 203:

﴿And remember Allah﴾ with the takbir (saying "Allahu akbar") at the stoning of the pillars (al-jamarat), ﴿during the appointed days﴾, that is, the three days of tashriq (the days of drying meat, 11th to 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah).

﴿Whoever hastens (taʿajjala) in two days﴾, that is, hurries to leave Mina (al-nafr min Mina), ﴿in two days﴾, that is, on the second of the days of tashriq after stoning its pillars, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾ for hastening.

﴿And whoever delays﴾ by it, until he spends the night of the third day and stones its pillars, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾ for that. That is, they have a choice in this, and the negation of sin applies ﴿to him who fears (Allah)﴾ in his pilgrimage, because he is the true pilgrim (al-hajj) in reality.

﴿And fear Allah, and know that you will be gathered unto Him﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and He will recompense you for your deeds﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 204:

﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the worldly life pleases you﴾ and does not please you in the Hereafter, because of its contradiction to what he believes. ﴿And he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾ that he agrees with what he says. ﴿Yet he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾ — most fierce in enmity toward you and your followers, because of his hostility toward you. He is al-Akhnas ibn Shariq. He was a hypocrite with sweet speech before the Prophet (ﷺ); he would swear that he believed in him and loved him, so the Prophet would bring him near to his gathering, and Allah refuted him in that. He passed by a field of crops and donkeys belonging to some of the Muslims, and he burned the crops and hamstrung the donkeys at night.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 205:

﴿When he turns away﴾ from you (انْصَرَفَ عَنْك), ﴿he strives﴾ walks (مَشى) ﴿in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy the crops and the progeny﴾, from among the forms of corruption, ﴿and Allah does not love corruption﴾, i.e., He does not approve of it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 206:

﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah,"﴾ in your conduct, ﴿pride takes hold of him﴾ arrogance and zealous self-regard carry him to act ﴿in sin﴾ which he was commanded to guard against. ﴿Hell will suffice him﴾ as sufficient for him. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾ the bed; it is Hell.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 207:

﴿And among the people is he who sells himself﴾ (yashri), i.e., gives himself (yabi'u nafsahu, i.e., he expends it) in obedience to God, ﴿seeking﴾ (ibtighā’) the pursuit of ﴿the pleasure of God﴾ (marḍāt Allāh), His good pleasure. This was Ṣuhayb, when the polytheists harmed him; he emigrated to Medina and left them his wealth. ﴿And God is Compassionate to the servants﴾ (ra’ūf bi-l-‘ibād), in that He guided them to what contains His pleasure.

It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions when they exalted Saturday and disliked camels after accepting Islam: ﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace⦅al-silm⦆ completely﴾ — with the sin pronounced with a fatḥa or a kasra — meaning Islam; ﴿completely⦅kaffah⦆﴾ is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of al-silm, i.e., in all its laws; ﴿and do not follow the footsteps⦅khuṭuwāt⦆ of Satan﴾ — i.e., paths — meaning his adornment of division; ﴿indeed, he is to you a clear enemy⦅mubīn⦆﴾ — evident in enmity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 209:

﴿Then if you slip﴾ turn away from entering into all of it, ﴿after the clear proofs have come to you﴾ the evident arguments showing that it is the truth, ﴿then know that Allah is Mighty﴾ nothing can frustrate Him from taking vengeance upon you, ﴿Wise﴾ in His creating.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 210:

﴿Are they waiting﴾ (هَلْ مَا يَنْظُرُونَ): what do those who refuse to enter into it await ﴿except that Allah should come to them﴾ (إلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ), i.e., His command, like His saying: ﴿or the command of your Lord comes﴾, i.e., His punishment ﴿in canopies﴾ (فِي ظُلَلٍ), plural of ẓullah (ظُلَّة), ﴿of clouds﴾ (مِنَ الْغَمَامِ), i.e., the clouds ﴿and the angels﴾ (وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ), ﴿and the matter is decided﴾ (وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ), i.e., the matter of their destruction is complete ﴿and to Allah all matters are returned﴾ (وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ), with the verb in the passive form and the agent in the Hereafter, so that He recompenses each person according to his deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (*Tafsir al-Jalalayn*) on surah 2, verse 211:

﴿Ask﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿the Children of Israel﴾, as a rebuke, ﴿how many signs We gave them﴾. Here كَمْ (*kam*, "how many") is an interrogative whose governing verb is suspended (*mu'allaqah*, i.e., the verb "ask" does not take it as a direct object), and it is the second object of آتَيْنا (*ataynā*, "We gave"). Its specifier (*mumayyiz*) is ﴿of a clear sign﴾, meaning manifest, such as the splitting of the sea and the sending down of the manna and the quails. But they replaced it with disbelief. ﴿And whoever substitutes the favour of Allah﴾, that is, what Allah has bestowed upon him of signs, because they are the means of guidance, ﴿after it has come to him﴾, by disbelief, ﴿then indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾ toward him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 212:

﴿Adorned for those who disbelieve is the life of this world﴾ — [this refers to] the people of Makkah — ﴿by deception, so they love it﴾; ﴿and﴾ they ﴿mock those who believe﴾ ﴿because of their poverty, such as Bilal, Ammar and Suhayb﴾, i.e., they ridicule them and look down upon them due to wealth. ﴿But those who fear [Allah]﴾ from shirk, and they are these [poor believers], ﴿will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾, i.e., abundant provision in the Hereafter or in this world, by which the mocked ones will come to own the wealth and the necks of those who mocked them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 213:

﴿Mankind was one community﴾ upon faith, then they differed, some believing and some disbelieving. ﴿So Allah sent the Prophets﴾ to them ﴿as bearers of good news﴾ to whoever believed, of Paradise, ﴿and as warners﴾ to whoever disbelieved, of the Fire. ﴿And He sent down with them the Book﴾ (meaning: the books) ﴿with the truth﴾ (related to "sent down") ﴿that it might judge﴾ by it ﴿between people concerning that in which they differed﴾ regarding the religion. ﴿And none differed concerning it﴾, i.e., the religion, ﴿except those who were given it﴾, i.e., the Book, so some believed and some disbelieved ﴿after the clear proofs had come to them﴾, the evident arguments for monotheism. "Min" (after) is related to "differed," and it and what follows it are, in meaning, placed before the exception. ﴿Out of rebellion﴾ from the disbelievers ﴿among themselves. Then Allah guided those who believed﴾ to ﴿the truth concerning that in which they differed﴾, where "min" is explanatory (lil-bayan), ﴿by His permission﴾, i.e., by His will. ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills﴾ to His guidance ﴿to a straight path﴾, the way of truth.

It was revealed concerning the hardship that afflicted the Muslims: "Or" (rather, "a") "did you think that you would enter Paradise while" (not) "there has yet come to you the example" (the likeness) "of those who passed away before you" (of the believers, of trials) "so that you might be patient as they were patient?" "Afflicted them" (a resumed sentence explaining what precedes it) "the misfortune" (the severity of poverty) "and the adversity" (illness) "and they were shaken" (they were disturbed by various kinds of tribulation) "until the Messenger and those who believed with him said" (with the verb in the accusative or the nominative, i.e., "said") "— ﴿and the Messenger and those who believed with him said﴾ — ﴿When will come the help of Allah?﴾" (a request for the help, because of the intensity of the hardship upon them) "When" (when will it come) "the help of Allah" (which we were promised), so they were answered from Allah: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾ (its coming).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 215:

﴿They ask you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿what they should spend﴾, i.e., what it is that they spend. The one asking was ʿAmr ibn al-Jamuh, who was an elderly man of wealth. So he asked (ﷺ) about what to spend and on whom to spend. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Whatever you spend of good﴾ is an explanation of "what", encompassing both the little and the much. In it is an explanation of the spender, which is one of the two parts of the question. He answered regarding the recipients, which is the other part, with His saying: ﴿for parents and relatives, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer﴾, i.e., they have the greater right to it. ﴿And whatever good you do﴾, whether spending or otherwise, ﴿indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾, so He will reward you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 216:

﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you﴾ (kutiba) means it was made obligatory, ﴿against the disbelievers﴾ (lil-kuffar), ﴿and it is hateful to you﴾ (wa-huwa kurh), meaning disliked (makruh), ﴿to you﴾ (lakum), meaning, in accordance with its hardship (tibqan li-mashaqqatihi). ﴿But it may be that you hate a thing and it is good for you, and it may be that you love a thing and it is bad for you.﴾ (wa-'asa an takrahu shay'an wa-huwa khayrun lakum wa-'asa an tuhibbu shay'an wa-huwa sharrun lakum) This is due to the soul's inclination toward desires that lead to its destruction, and its aversion from the obligations that lead to its happiness. So perhaps there is good for you in fighting, even though you dislike it, because in it is either victory and spoils, or martyrdom and reward; and in abandoning it, even though you love it, there is evil, because in it is humiliation, poverty and the loss of reward. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ what is good for you, ﴿while you do not know﴾ that, so hasten to do what He commands you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 217:

The Prophet (ﷺ) sent out his first expedition (sariyyah), under the command of ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh. They fought the polytheists and killed Ibn al-Hadrami on the last day of Jumada al-Akhirah, and it became confused for them (that it might be) Rajab. So the disbelievers reproached them for making it lawful (to fight in a sacred month), and there was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, concerning fighting in it.﴾ (The word "the sacred month" is) the forbidden (month), and "fighting in it" is a substitute (badal ishtimal). ﴿Say:﴾ to them, ﴿"Fighting in it is a great sin"﴾, great in burden (wizr), a subject and predicate (mubtada' wa khabar). ﴿And hindering﴾ (ṣadd), a subject (mubtada'), meaning preventing people ﴿from the way of God﴾, His religion, ﴿and disbelief in Him﴾, in God, ﴿and (hindering access to) the Sacred Mosque﴾, that is, Mecca, ﴿and expelling its people from it﴾, and they are the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers. The predicate of the subject is ﴿greater﴾, more grave in burden, ﴿in the sight of God﴾ than fighting in it. ﴿And persecution﴾, that is, polytheism, from you, ﴿is greater than killing﴾ on your part in it. ﴿And they will not cease﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿fighting you﴾, O believers, ﴿until﴾ (so that, kay), ﴿they turn you back from your religion﴾ to disbelief, ﴿if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever, those—their deeds have become worthless﴾, they have been nullified, ﴿in this world and the Hereafter﴾, so they carry no weight and no reward is given for them. The restriction to dying in that state indicates that if he returns to Islam, his deed is not nullified, so he is rewarded for it and does not have to repeat it, such as the Hajj, for example. Al-Shafiʿi held this view. ﴿And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

When the expedition (al-sariyya) thought that, if they were spared sin, they would not earn a reward, this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated﴾ left their homelands, ﴿and have striven in the way of Allah﴾ to raise high His religion, ﴿those hope for the mercy of Allah﴾ His reward. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ to the believers ﴿and Merciful﴾ toward them.

They ask you about wine and gambling. (﴿يَسْأَلُونَك عَنْ الخَمْر والمَيْسِر﴾) Gambling (al-qimar) and what has the same ruling as it.

Say, ﴿In them is a great sin﴾, that is, in indulging in them, and ﴿great﴾ means severe. In one recitation (qira'a) with the letter thāʾ (ث), it reads as "much," referring to what results from them of quarrelling, mutual abuse and foul speech. ﴿And [there are] benefits for people﴾: in wine, pleasure and joy; in gambling, gaining wealth without toil. ﴿But their sin is greater than their benefit﴾, that is, the corruptions that arise from them are greater. ﴿Greater﴾ means more severe.

When this verse was revealed, some people drank wine and others abstained from it, until the verse of Surat al-Maʾidah prohibited it.

﴿And they ask you what they should spend﴾, that is, how much. ﴿Say: spend the surplus (al-ʿafw)﴾, that is, what is left over beyond your need, and do not spend what you need and so ruin yourselves. In one recitation with the nominative vowel (raf'), by supposing the implied subject "huwa" (it), it reads "al-ʿafw is [what you spend]." ﴿Thus﴾, that is, just as what has been mentioned has been made clear to you, ﴿Allah makes clear to you the signs so that you may reflect﴾.

fī (concerning) the affair of this world and the Hereafter, so that you take what is most beneficial for you in both. ﴿And they ask you about orphans.﴾ and what hardship they face concerning their affairs: if they eat with them, they sin; and if they separate their property from theirs and prepare food for them alone, that is a hardship. ﴿Say: Setting things right for them﴾ in their property, by developing it and mixing with them, ﴿is good﴾, good compared with leaving that alone. ﴿And if you mix with them﴾, i.e., mix your expenses with theirs, ﴿then they are your brothers﴾, i.e., they are your brothers in religion, and it is the nature of a brother to mix with his brother; so that is permitted for you. ﴿And God knows the corrupter﴾ of their property by mixing with it ﴿from the one who sets things right﴾ with it, so He will recompense each of the two. ﴿And had God willed, He would have burdened you﴾, i.e., He would have restricted you by forbidding mixing. ﴿Indeed God is Mighty﴾, prevailing over His command, ﴿Wise﴾ in His creation.

﴿And do not marry﴾ (tatazawwajū), O Muslims, ﴿the polytheistic women﴾, that is, the disbelieving women, ﴿until they believe. And a believing slave-woman is better than a polytheist﴾, a free woman, because the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) was the reproach directed at one who married a slave-woman and his preference for marrying a free polytheist woman. ﴿Even though she pleases you﴾ for her beauty and her wealth. This is restricted to other than the women of the Book, by the verse ﴿and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture﴾. ﴿And do not marry﴾ (tuzawwijū) ﴿the polytheist men﴾, that is, the disbelievers, to the believing women, ﴿until they believe. And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he pleases you﴾ for his wealth and his beauty. ﴿Those﴾, that is, the people of polytheism, ﴿invite to the Fire﴾ by their calling to the deed that necessitates it, so marriage with them is not fitting. ﴿But Allah invites﴾ through the tongue of His messengers ﴿to Paradise and forgiveness﴾, that is, to the deed that necessitates them, ﴿by His permission﴾, by His will, so responding to Him by marrying His friends (awliyā') is obligatory. ﴿And He makes His signs clear to the people, that they may remember﴾, that they may take heed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 222:

﴿They ask you about menstruation.﴾ That is, about menstruation (al-hayd) or its place: what should be done with women during it? ﴿Say: It is an injury.﴾ That is, filth; or its location is the injury. ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation.﴾ That is, leave off having intercourse with them. ﴿During menstruation﴾ means during its time or its place. ﴿And do not approach them﴾ by intercourse ﴿until they are purified.﴾ It is read with the taa' sukoon and with shaddah on the taa', and the haa' is also read; in the original form the taa' (of tatahhurna) is assimilated into the taa' (of the verb), i.e., until they wash themselves after its cessation. ﴿But when they have purified themselves, then come to them﴾ by intercourse ﴿in the manner which Allah has ordained for you.﴾ That is, by avoiding it during menstruation, and it is the front passage (al-qubul); do not transgress it to other than it. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves﴾ that is, rewards and honours ﴿those who are constantly repentant﴾ from sins ﴿and loves those who purify themselves﴾ from impurities.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 223:

﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, i.e., a place for the sowing of your seed, the child. ﴿So go to your tilth﴾, i.e., its place, which is the front passage (al-qubul). ﴿How you will﴾, i.e., how ⟨you wish⟩, ﴿standing, sitting, lying down, from the front or from behind﴾.
