It was revealed in response to the saying of the Jews: whoever has intercourse with his wife in her front passage from behind, the child will be born cross-eyed. ﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾, i.e., righteous deeds, such as saying the basmala (tasmiya) at intercourse. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ in His commands and prohibitions. ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾ through resurrection, so He will recompense you for your deeds. ﴿And give good news to the believers﴾ who have feared Him, of Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 224:

﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle [ʿurḍah] for your oaths﴾ — i.e., do not make the swearing by Him a barrier ('illah māni'ah) to your oaths, i.e., a target (naṣban) for them, by swearing by Him so frequently ﴿that﴾ you do not ﴿act righteously and fear Allah﴾, so that the oath is disliked in that case, and breaking it (al-ḥinth) is recommended (yusann), and one expiates it. Contrary to that, [the oath is preferable] for performing righteousness and the like, so it is obedience. ﴿And make peace between people﴾. The meaning: do not refrain from doing what has been mentioned of righteousness and the like when you have sworn to it; rather, go and do it and make expiation, because the reason for its revelation was refraining from that. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of your statements, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of your conditions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 225:

﴿Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, which is what the tongue utters without intending to swear, such as "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah"; there is no sin for it and no expiation. ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾, i.e., what you intended of oaths when you break them. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ of what occurred of the unintentional (laghw), ﴿Forbearing﴾, by delaying punishment beyond the one who deserves it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 226:

﴿For those who swear off their wives﴾ means: who swear that they will not have intercourse with them. ﴿a waiting of four months﴾ means: a waiting period. ﴿Then if they return﴾ means: they revert, within it or after it, from the oath to intercourse. ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving﴾ so He will be forgiving to them for what they did of harm to the woman by the oath. ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them.

﴿And if they resolve on divorce﴾, meaning: upon it, by not returning (to their wives). Then let them pronounce it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾ of their words, ﴿Knowing﴾ of their resolve. The meaning: after the waiting period that was mentioned, they have only two options: returning (al-fay'ah) or divorce (al-talaq).

﴿The divorced women shall wait﴾, i.e., let them wait, ﴿by themselves﴾, by themselves, from marriage, ﴿for three periods﴾ (*qurū'*), passing from the time of the divorce. *Qurū'* is the plural of *qar'* (*qarʾ*, with a fatḥa on the qāf), which means either purity (*ṭuhr*) or menstruation (*ḥayḍ*), there being two opinions. This applies to women who have been consummated with. As for others, there is no waiting period (*ʿiddah*) for them, due to His words: ﴿you have no waiting period for them to count﴾. For women who are neither past menopause nor young, their waiting period is three months. For pregnant women, it is until they give birth to their load, as in Surat al-Ṭalāq. For slave women, their waiting period is two *qurū'*, according to the Sunnah. ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾, of children and menstruation, ﴿if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back﴾, to resume their marriage with them, ﴿even if they have been divorced in that period﴾, i.e., during the waiting period, ﴿if they desire reconciliation﴾ between them, because of harm to the woman. This is an exhortation to its intent, not a condition for the validity of the taking back. This applies to revocable divorce (*rajʿī*). The word *aḥaqq* (more entitled) does not imply a comparison here, since no one else has a right to marry them during the waiting period. ﴿And they have rights similar to those they have﴾, over the husbands, ﴿of what is reasonable﴾, as defined by the Sharīʿah, of good companionship, avoiding harm, and the like. ﴿But men have a degree over them﴾, a superiority in rights, namely the obligation of their obedience to them, because of what they have given of the dower and maintenance. ﴿And Allah is Almighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He has ordained for His creation.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 2, verse 229:**

﴿The divorce﴾ means the pronouncement of divorce after which reconciliation is possible. ﴿Twice﴾ means two times. ﴿Then retain [them] in kindness﴾ means it is incumbent upon you to retain them after that by taking them back ﴿with kindness﴾, without harm. ﴿Or release [them] with good treatment﴾ means to let them go ﴿with good treatment﴾. ﴿And it is not lawful for you﴾, O husbands, ﴿to take back anything of what you have given them﴾ of the dowries ﴿if you divorce them﴾, ﴿except when both fear﴾ meaning the spouses fear ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, meaning that they will not fulfil what Allah has prescribed for them of rights. In another recitation, it is read as ﴿yakhafa﴾ (in the passive voice), so that ﴿an-la yuqeema﴾ is a substitute (badal al-ishtimal) for the pronoun in it. It is also recited with the second-person prefix (al-fawqaniyya) in both verbs. ﴿And if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them﴾ ﴿for what she gives up to be released﴾, meaning the wealth she pays in order that he divorce her. That is, there is no sin upon the husband in taking it, nor upon the wife in giving it. ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah — it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Then if he divorces her﴾, the husband, after the two (pronouncements), ﴿then she is not lawful for him thereafter﴾, after the third pronouncement, ﴿until she marries﴾ (tatazawwaj, marries) ﴿another husband﴾ and he has intercourse with her (yatai'ha), as in the hadith related by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim). ﴿Then if he divorces her﴾, that is, the second husband, ﴿there is no blame on either of them﴾, that is, the wife and the first husband, ﴿if they return to one another﴾ in marriage after the completion of the 'iddah (waiting period). ﴿If they think they can keep within the limits of Allah﴾. ﴿And these﴾, the aforementioned matters, ﴿are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear to a people who know﴾, who reflect (yatadabbarun).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 231:

﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term﴾ meaning, they approach the end of their waiting period (ʿiddah) ﴿then retain them﴾ by taking them back ﴿with kindness﴾ without harm ﴿or release them with kindness﴾ leave them until their waiting period ends ﴿And do not retain them﴾ by taking them back ﴿to harm them﴾ (ḍirāran) is an object of purpose ﴿so that you transgress﴾ against them by compelling them to ransom themselves (iftidāʾ) and to divorce, and by prolonging the confinement ﴿And whoever does that has wronged himself﴾ by exposing himself to the punishment of Allah ﴿And do not take the signs of Allah in mockery﴾ mocked by disobeying them ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ by Islam ﴿and what He has sent down to you of the Book﴾ the Qur'an ﴿and the wisdom﴾ what it contains of rulings ﴿He admonishes you thereby﴾ by your thanking Him through acting upon it ﴿And fear Allah, and know that Allah is Knower of all things﴾ and nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 232:

﴿And when you divorce women and they have reached their term﴾ (i.e., their waiting period has ended), ﴿do not prevent them﴾ — this is an address to the guardians (awliya'), meaning: do not hinder them ﴿from marrying their husbands﴾ — the ones who had divorced them — because the occasion of its revelation was that the sister of Ma'qil ibn Yasar was divorced by her husband, then he wished to take her back, but Ma'qil ibn Yasar prevented her, as narrated by al-Hakim. ﴿When they agree among themselves in a reasonable manner﴾ — i.e., the husbands and the women — ﴿in a manner recognized by the Sharia﴾. ﴿This﴾ prohibition of obstruction ﴿is an admonition for whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾, because he is the one who benefits from it. ﴿That﴾ — i.e., abandoning obstruction — ﴿is better for you and purer﴾ for you and for them, because of what is feared for the couple of suspicion arising from the relationship between them. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ what contains the benefit, ﴿and you do not know﴾ that, so follow His commands.

﴿And mothers shall suckle﴾, i.e., *li-yurḍi'na* (they should suckle), ﴿their children for two full years﴾, i.e., *ʿāmayn* (two years), ﴿kāmilayn﴾ (full), a *ṣifa muʾakkada* (an emphasizing qualifier) — ﴿that is for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾, and there is no addition beyond it. ﴿And upon the one to whom the child belongs﴾, i.e., the father, ﴿is their provision﴾, meaning the feeding of the mothers, ﴿and their clothing﴾ for the nursing, if they are divorced, ﴿according to what is fair﴾, i.e., according to his capacity. ﴿No soul is burdened except according to its capacity﴾, i.e., its ability. ﴿No mother shall be harmed because of her child﴾, i.e., on account of it, by being forced to nurse it if she refuses. ﴿Nor shall a father be harmed because of his child﴾, i.e., on account of it, by being burdened beyond his capacity. The attribution of "child" to each of them in both places is for the purpose of *istiʿṭāf* (eliciting compassion). ﴿And upon the heir﴾, i.e., the heir of the father, who is the infant, meaning upon his guardian from his property, ﴿is the like of that﴾, which is incumbent upon the father toward the mother, of provision and clothing. ﴿If the two of them wish﴾, i.e., the parents, ﴿weaning﴾, i.e., cessation of nursing before the two years, ﴿arising from mutual consent﴾, i.e., agreement, ﴿between them and consultation﴾ between them, so that the child's interest in it becomes evident, ﴿then there is no blame upon them both﴾ in that. ﴿And if you wish﴾, addressing the fathers, ﴿to seek wet-nurses for your children﴾, i.e., nurses other than the mothers, ﴿then there is no blame upon you﴾ in that, ﴿provided you hand over﴾ to them ﴿what you have given﴾, i.e., what you intend to give them of the wage, ﴿according to what is fair﴾, i.e., with kindness, such as good-heartedness. ﴿And fear God, and know that God is Seeing of what you do﴾, nothing of it being hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 234:

﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾ die, ﴿they shall wait for themselves﴾, that is, they shall wait (li-yatarabbaṣna), ﴿for four months and ten days﴾ of nights, from their husbands' death, abstaining from marriage. This applies to women who are not pregnant; as for pregnant women, their waiting period is until they give birth to their load, by the verse of divorce (āyat al-ṭalāq). A slave woman's period is half of that, by the Sunnah. ﴿When they have reached their term﴾, meaning the period of their waiting has ended, ﴿there is no blame upon you, O guardians﴾, ﴿for what they do with themselves﴾ of adornment and presenting themselves to suitors ﴿in an acceptable manner﴾ according to the Sharia, ﴿and Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, knowing its inward as well as its outward aspects.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah al-Baqarah, verse 235:**

﴿There is no blame upon you for what you allude to﴾ (*lawwahtum*, you hint) ﴿of the proposal to women﴾ (*khitbah*, a proposal of marriage) ﴿whose husbands have died, during their waiting period, such as a person saying: "Indeed, you are beautiful," "Whoever finds someone like you," or "Many a man desires you."﴾ ﴿Or what you conceal﴾ (*admartum*, you harbour) ﴿within yourselves﴾ of the intention to marry them. ﴿Allah knows that you will remember them﴾ with a proposal, and that you cannot restrain yourselves from them. So He permitted you the allusion. ﴿But do not promise them secretly﴾, i.e., marriage, ﴿except﴾ (i.e., but) ﴿that you say a fair word﴾, i.e., what is known in the Shariah of allusion; for you are permitted that. ﴿And do not determine the tie of marriage﴾, i.e., do not resolve upon its contract, ﴿until the prescribed term reaches its end﴾, i.e., the written period of the waiting period ﴿reaches its appointed time﴾, by its completion. ﴿And know that Allah knows what is within your selves﴾ of resolve and other things. ﴿So beware of Him﴾, lest He punish you if you resolve. ﴿And know that Allah is Forgiving﴾ to whoever fears Him, ﴿Forbearing﴾, in delaying punishment beyond its deserving.

(Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 2, verse 236:

﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them﴾. In another recitation (qira'a, a variant mode of reading the Qur'an), it is read as (تُماسُّوهُنَّ, tumassūhunna), meaning: you have not had intercourse with them. The word (ما, mā) is a verbal-noun particle functioning as a time adverb, meaning: there is no liability upon you in divorcing them during the time when you have not touched them, nor any dowry, and so divorce them. ﴿Or﴾ you have not ﴿specified for them a obligatory portion﴾, meaning a dowry, ﴿and provide for them﴾, meaning give them what they may enjoy. ﴿According to the wealthy among you﴾, meaning the affluent, ﴿his means, and according to the straitened﴾, meaning the one whose provision is restricted, ﴿his means﴾. This indicates that no consideration is given to the wife's own means. ﴿A provision﴾, meaning a provision of enjoyment, ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾, meaning according to the Shari'a. (مَتاعًا, matā'an) is a qualifier of the word "provision". ﴿A duty﴾ (حَقًّا, ḥaqqan) is a second qualifier, or a verbal noun serving as an emphasis. ﴿Upon the doers of good﴾, meaning the obedient.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 237:

﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already appointed for them a dowry, then half of what you have appointed⁠﴾ is due to them, and half returns to you. ﴿Unless⁠﴾ (i.e., but rather) ﴿they forgo⁠﴾ (i.e., the wives, so they give it up) ﴿or he in whose hand is the marriage tie⁠﴾, who is the husband, so that he leaves her the whole. And from Ibn ʿAbbas: it is the guardian (walī), if she is under guardianship (maḥjūrah), then there is no blame in that. ﴿And that you forgo is nearer to piety⁠﴾, a subject whose predicate is ﴿nearer to piety⁠﴾. ﴿And do not forget graciousness between you⁠﴾, i.e., that some of you show favour to others. ﴿Indeed Allah is Seeing of what you do⁠﴾, so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 238:

﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾, the five, by performing them at their appointed times. ﴿And the middle prayer﴾ is the ʿAṣr (afternoon prayer), or the Ṣubḥ (dawn prayer), or the Ẓuhr (noon prayer), or other than these; there are opinions. He singled it out for mention because of its excellence. ﴿And stand before Allah﴾ in prayer ﴿devoutly obedient﴾. It was said: obedient, based on his statement ﷺ: "Every qunūt in the Qur'an is obedience," narrated by Aḥmad and others. And it was said: silent, based on the ḥadīth of Zayd ibn Arqam: "We used to speak in prayer until this was revealed, and we were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak," narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 239:

﴿And if you fear﴾ from an enemy, or a torrent, or a beast of prey, ﴿then on foot﴾ — "rijal" is the plural of "rajil," meaning on foot, i.e., pray ﴿or riding﴾ — "rukban" is the plural of "rakib," meaning however it is possible, facing the qiblah or not, and gesturing with the bowing and the prostration. ﴿And when you are safe﴾ from fear, ﴿then remember God﴾, i.e., pray ﴿as He taught you what you did not know﴾ before He taught you it, of its obligations and its rights. The kaf (ka) here means "like," and ma is either a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah) or a relative pronoun (mawsulah).

﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾ [let them make a bequest], ﴿a bequest﴾. In one qira'a (recitation), it is read in the nominative, meaning ﴿upon them﴾, i.e. [it is incumbent] ﴿for their wives﴾, and ﴿let them provide for them﴾ ﴿a provision﴾, meaning what they may benefit from of maintenance and clothing, ﴿until﴾ the completion of ﴿the year﴾ [as a] hal (circumstantial qualifier), meaning, ﴿not expelling them from their dwellings﴾. ﴿But if they leave﴾ of their own accord, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, O guardians of the deceased, ﴿for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾ according to the Sharia, such as adorning themselves, abandoning mourning (ihdad, the mourning period), and cutting off maintenance from them. ﴿And Allah is Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿Wise﴾ in His creation. The bequest mentioned has been abrogated (naskh, abrogation) by the verse of inheritance, and the waiting period of a year has been abrogated by the verse of ﴿four months and ten days﴾, which came earlier in revelation but later in recitation. Residence (al-sukna) for them remains valid according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 241:

﴿And for divorced women there is provision﴾ they shall give it ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾ according to what is within capability ﴿as a duty﴾ it is in the accusative, governed by its implied verb ﴿upon the God-fearing﴾ Allah, exalted is He, repeated it so that it would include also the woman who has been touched (consummated), since the preceding verse concerns other than her.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 242:

﴿Thus﴾ as He has made clear to you what has been mentioned, ﴿Allah makes His signs clear to you, so that you may understand﴾ [that is, that you may] reflect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 243:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ is an interrogative of wonder and eager anticipation, directed toward listening to what follows; i.e., let your knowledge reach ﴿to those who went out from their homes, and they were thousands﴾, four thousand, or eight thousand, or ten thousand, or thirty thousand, or forty thousand, or seventy thousand, ﴿fearing death﴾, a object of purpose (maf'ul lahu). They were a people from the Children of Israel, among whom the plague (ta'un) had struck their land, so they fled. ﴿Then God said to them, "Die," and they died﴾. ﴿Then He brought them to life﴾ after eight days or more, through the supplication of their prophet Ezekiel (Hizqil), pronounced with a kasra on the unmarked ha, a qaf, and a silent zay. They lived for a long time with the traces of death upon them: whenever they wore a garment, it became like a shroud. And this continued among their descendants. ﴿Indeed, God is bounteous toward mankind﴾, and among that bounty is the revival of these people. ﴿But most of mankind﴾, namely the disbelievers, ﴿do not give thanks﴾. The purpose of mentioning the story of these people is to encourage the believers to fight, and therefore it is connected to what follows.
ﷻ"Fight in the way of Allah" — that is, to raise high His religion. "And know that Allah is All-Hearing" of your statements, "All-Knowing" of your conditions, so He will recompense you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 245:

﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾ by spending his wealth in the way of Allah, ﴿a goodly loan﴾ by spending it sincerely, with a willing heart, ﴿so that He may multiply it for him manifold﴾ — in another reading, fa-yudaˁʻifahu (with the doubling of the ʻayn) — ﴿many times over﴾, from ten up to more than seven hundred, as will come later. ﴿And Allah withholds and extends﴾ — He withholds provision from whom He wills as a trial, ﴿and extends﴾ it, He widens it for whom He wills as a test. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ in the Hereafter, through resurrection, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 246:

﴿Have you not considered the chiefs﴾ — the assembly — i.e., their story and account, ﴿of the Children of Israel, after Moses﴾ — after the death of Moses — i.e., their story and account, ﴿when they said to a prophet of theirs﴾ — he was Shamwil (Samuel) — ﴿"Appoint for us a king﴾ — set up — ﴿that we may fight﴾ with him ﴿in the way of Allah,"﴾ by which our word will be united and we will return to him. ﴿He said﴾ — the Prophet said to them — ﴿"Is it possible that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?"﴾ — ʿasaytum, with fath and kasr (ʿasaytum / ʿasītum) — ﴿in that [if] you will not fight﴾ is the predicate of ʿasā, and the interrogative is for confirming the expectation with it. ﴿They said, "And why should we not fight in the way of Allah, when we have been driven out of our homes and our children?"﴾ — by their being taken captive and killed; the people of Jalut (Goliath) had indeed done that to them — i.e., there is no impediment for us to it while its motive exists. ﴿But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away﴾ — they turned away from it and were cowardly — ﴿except a few of them﴾ — and they were those who crossed the river with Talut (Saul), as will come. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ — so He will recompense them. He [the Prophet] had asked for the sending of a king, and He answered him by sending Talut.

﴿Their prophet said to them, "Indeed, Allah has sent Talut (Saul) as a king for you." They said, "How" (أنّى, meaning "how") ﴾ "can he" (كَيْفَ, meaning "how") ﴿have kingship over us, when we are more deserving of kingship than him?﴾ Because he is not from the lineage (sibt) of the royal family nor of prophethood, and he was a tanner or a shepherd. ﴿And he was not given abundant wealth,﴾ by which he could be helped in establishing the kingship. ﴿He said﴾ the Prophet to them, ﴿"Indeed, Allah has chosen him﴾ selected him for kingship ﴿over you, and has increased him in breadth﴾ abundance ﴿of knowledge and physique,"﴾ and he was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel at that time, the most handsome of them, and the most perfect of them in creation. ﴿And Allah gives His kingship to whom He wills﴾ giving it to him is not open to objection. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing﴾ in His bounty, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of who is worthy of it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 248:

﴿And their Prophet said to them﴾ when they asked him for a sign of his kingship, ﴿Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that there will come to you the chest (tabut)﴾ the box in which were pictures of the prophets. It was sent down to Adam and was passed down to them. The Amalekites overcame them, seized it, and they used to seek victory through it over their enemy, put it forward in battle, and find tranquility in it, ﴿in it is tranquility﴾ reassurance for your hearts ﴿from your Lord, and a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind﴾ which were the sandals of Musa, his staff, the turban of Harun, a qafiz (measure) of the manna that used to descend upon them, and fragments of the tablets. ﴿The angels will carry it﴾ a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the subject of "will come to you". ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for you﴾ of his kingship ﴿if you are believers﴾. So the angels carried it between the heavens and the earth while they looked at it, until they placed it before Talut (Saul). Then they acknowledged his kingship, hastened to jihad, and he chose seventy thousand of their youth.

﴿When he set out﴾ means Talut (Saul) went out with the troops from Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). The heat was intense, and they asked him for water. ﴿He said, "Indeed Allah is going to test you﴾ (yukhtabiruka, i.e., examine you) ﴿with a river,"﴾ so that the obedient among you would be distinguished from the disobedient. It lies between al-Urdunn (Jordan) and Filastin (Palestine). ﴿Whoever drinks from it﴾ (i.e., from its water) ﴿is not of me﴾ (i.e., not of my followers), ﴿and whoever does not taste it﴾ (yadhuqhu, i.e., does not drink from it) ﴿is indeed of me, except one who scoops up a handful﴾ (ghurfa, written غُرْفَة, pronounced with the ghayn vowelled either with fatha, غَرْفَة, or with damma, غُرْفَة) ﴿with his hand﴾, and is content with it and does not exceed it, for he is of me. ﴿So they drank from it﴾ when they came to it in large numbers, ﴿except a few of them﴾, who limited themselves to the handful. It is related that it sufficed them for drinking and for their animals, and they numbered three hundred and some ten men (bid'a 'ashar, i.e., around thirteen).

﴿When he and those who believed with him had crossed it﴾, namely those who had limited themselves to the handful, ﴿they said﴾ (i.e., those who had drunk), ﴿"We have no strength﴾ (taqa, i.e., power) ﴿today against Jalut and his troops"﴾ (i.e., to fight them), and they became cowardly and did not cross it. ﴿Those who were certain﴾ (yazunnuna, i.e., were certain) ﴿that they would meet Allah﴾ on the Resurrection, and they were the ones who had crossed it, ﴿said﴾: ﴿"How many﴾ (kam, a khabariyya, meaning "many") ﴿a small company﴾ (fi'a, i.e., group) ﴿has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah﴾ (bi-idhnihi, i.e., by His will)! ﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾ with His help and victory.

When they went forth to Goliath and his troops, (﻿ﷻ) that is, they appeared for battle and lined up in ranks, they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and make firm our feet﴾ (aṣbib: pour down), by strengthening our hearts for jihad, ﴿and help us against the disbelieving people.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 251:

﴿So they routed them﴾ broke them, ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾ by His will, ﴿and Dawud killed﴾ and he was in the army of Talut ﴿Jalut. And Allah gave him﴾ i.e. Dawud ﴿the kingdom﴾ among the Children of Israel ﴿and wisdom﴾ prophethood after the death of Shamwil (Samuel) and Talut, and these two had not been combined for anyone before him ﴿and taught him﴾ ﴿of what He willed﴾ such as the craft of making coats of mail and the speech of birds ﴿And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others﴾ instead of some of the people ﴿by others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾ by the victory of the polytheists, the killing of the Muslims and the destruction of the mosques ﴿but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds﴾ so He repelled some of them by means of others.

﴿That﴾ means these ﴿verses﴾ (ayat), ﴿the verses of Allah, We recite them﴾, meaning We relate them, ﴿to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿in truth﴾, meaning in truthfulness, ﴿and indeed you are among the messengers﴾. The emphasis (ta'kid) with ﴿indeed﴾ (inna) and the other particles is a refutation of the disbelievers' saying to him, "You are not a messenger."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 253:

﴿تِلْكَ﴾ ("Those") is the mubtada' (subject of the nominal sentence). ﴿الرُّسُل﴾ ("the Messengers") is either a na't (qualifying adjective) or an 'atf bayan (explanatory apposition). The khabar (predicate) is ﴿فَضَّلْنا بَعْضهمْ عَلى بَعْض﴾ ("We made some of them exceed others"), by singling out each one with a distinction that was not given to anyone else. ﴿مِنهُمْ مَن كَلَّمَ اللَّه﴾ ("Among them are those to whom Allah spoke") refers to Musa. ﴿ورَفَعَ بَعْضهمْ﴾ ("and raised some of them") refers to Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿دَرَجات﴾ ("in degrees") above others, through the universality of his call, the sealing of prophethood, the superiority of his community over all other nations, his numerous miracles, and his many distinctive features. ﴿وآتَيْنا عِيسى ابْن مَرْيَم البَيِّنات وأَيَّدْناهُ﴾ ("And We gave Isa, son of Maryam, the clear proofs and strengthened him") means "We empowered him" ﴿بِرُوحِ القُدُس﴾ ("with the Holy Spirit"), meaning Jibril, who accompanied him wherever he went. ﴿ولَوْ شاءَ اللَّه﴾ ("Had Allah willed") to guide all people, ﴿ما اقْتَتَلَ الَّذِينَ مِن بَعْدهمْ﴾ ("those who came after them would not have fought each other"), meaning their nations after the Messengers, ﴿مِن بَعْد ما جاءَتْهُمْ البَيِّنات﴾ ("after the clear proofs had come to them"), because of their disagreement and their misleading of one another. ﴿ولَكِنْ اخْتَلَفُوا﴾ ("But they differed") by His will for that. ﴿فَمِنهُمْ مَن آمَنَ﴾ ("Among them were those who believed") and remained steadfast in their faith, ﴿ومِنهُمْ مَن كَفَرَ﴾ ("and among them were those who disbelieved"), such as the Christians after al-Masih. ﴿ولَوْ شاءَ اللَّه ما اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ ("Had Allah willed, they would not have fought") is a repetition for emphasis. ﴿ولَكِنَّ اللَّه يَفْعَل ما يُرِيد﴾ ("But Allah does what He wills"), granting success to whomever He wills and abandoning whomever He wills.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 254:

﴿O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided for you﴾ [of] its zakat, ﴿before there comes a Day in which there is no trade﴾ (i.e., ransom) ﴿nor friendship﴾ (i.e., companionship that benefits) ﴿nor intercession﴾ without His permission. That is the Day of Resurrection. In another reading, the three are in the nominative case [i.e., "no trade, no friendship, no intercession" are read as "lā bay'un, lā khullatun, lā shafā'atun" with tanwīn of raf'].

﴿And the disbelievers﴾ in Allah, or in what has been enjoined upon them, ﴿they are the wrongdoers﴾, because they place the command of Allah in other than its proper place.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, a classical exegesis) on Surah 2, verse 255:

﴿Allah, there is no god﴾ meaning, there is no one truly worthy of worship in existence, ﴿except Him, the Living﴾ who endures with everlasting life, ﴿the Self-Subsisting﴾ who is most intensive in sustaining the management of His creation. ﴿Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep.﴾ Slumber. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in dominion, creation, and servitude. ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ meaning, no one, unless He grants permission for it. ﴿He knows what is before them﴾ meaning, the creatures, ﴿and what is behind them﴾ meaning, the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And they encompass nothing of His knowledge﴾ meaning, they know nothing of what is known to Him ﴿except for what He wills﴾ to make them know of it through the reports of the messengers. ﴿His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.﴾ It was said that His knowledge encompasses them both, and it was said that the Kursi itself encompasses them, owing to its greatness, based on the hadith: (The seven heavens within the Kursi are nothing but seven dirhams cast into a shield). ﴿And their preservation does not tire Him﴾ does not burden Him, ﴿and He is the Most High﴾ above His creation by dominance, ﴿the Most Great﴾ the Magnificent.

﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾ to enter it. ﴿The right course has become clear from error﴾, i.e., it has become manifest through the clear signs that faith is right guidance and disbelief is error. It was revealed concerning a man among the Ansar (the Helpers) who had sons and wanted to compel them to embrace Islam. ﴿So whoever disbelieves in the Taghut﴾, i.e., Satan or the idols, a term that applies to both the singular and the plural, ﴿and believes in God, has grasped﴾ held fast ﴿to the firmest handhold﴾ the firm bond ﴿that will never break﴾ severance ﴿from it. And God is All-Hearing﴾ of what is said ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what is done.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 257:

﴿Allah is the Walī (protector, helper) of those who believe; He brings them out of the darkness (kufr, disbelief) into the light (īmān, faith). And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Ṭāghūt (false deities, every object of worship besides Allah); they bring them out of the light into the darkness.﴾ He mentioned "bringing out" either in contrast to His saying "He brings them out of the darkness," or it refers to everyone who believed in the Prophet before his mission (baʿthah) from among the Jews, then disbelieved in him. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 258:

﴿Have you not considered the one who argued﴾ disputed (ḥājja) ﴿with Abraham about his Lord﴾ ﴿because Allah had given him the kingdom﴾ i.e., his arrogance, through the blessing of Allah, drove him to that, and he was Nimrod (Numrūdh). ﴿When﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "argued." ﴿Abraham said﴾ when he said to him, "Who is your Lord to whom you invite us?" ﴿My Lord is the One who gives life and causes death﴾ i.e., He creates life and death in bodies. ﴿He said﴾ it is ﴿"I give life and cause death"﴾ by killing and pardoning. He summoned two men, killed one and left the other alive. When [Abraham] saw that he was dull-witted, ﴿Abraham said﴾ moving on to a clearer proof than it: ﴿"Indeed Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west,"﴾ you ﴿"from the west." So the one who disbelieved was confounded﴾ bewildered and dumbfounded. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ who disbelieve, to the path (maḥajja) of argument.

Or [have you not considered] like the one who passed by a town, [the Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)], riding a donkey, with a basket of figs and a jug of juice with him, and he was Uzair (Ezra). And it was fallen upon its roofs (khawiya: fallen down), [i.e., its roofs had collapsed] when Bukhtanassar (Nebuchadnezzar) had ruined it. He said, "How will Allah give life to this [town] after its death?" (out of magnifying His power, exalted is He). So Allah caused him to die, and kept him dead for a hundred years; then He raised him, [brought him back to life], to show him how that would be. He said, [Allah, exalted is He, said to him], "How long have you remained?" [i.e., here]. He said, "I have remained a day or part of a day," because he had slept at the beginning of the day, and was taken [in death], and was brought back to life at sunset, so he thought it was the day he slept. He said, "Nay, you have remained a hundred years. Look at your food and your drink, [the figs and the juice], which has not spoiled (lam yatasannah) [i.e., it has not changed over the long passage of time]. The ha' in it is said to be original, from sanaht, and it is said to be for pause, from sanayt. In one reading it is recited with the ha' omitted. And look at your donkey, [how it is]; so he saw it dead, and its bones white and shining. And that We may make you a sign to the people [of resurrection]. And look at the bones, [of your donkey], how We raise them (nunshizuha): We give them life; it is read with a damma on the nun, and it is read with a fatha, from anshaza and nasaza, both being dialects; and in one reading with a damma on it and a zay: We move them and lift them up. Then We clothe them with flesh; so he looked at it, and it had been assembled, clothed with flesh, the spirit had been breathed into it, and it brayed. When it became clear to him, [that is, by direct witnessing], he said, "I know, [with knowledge gained by witnessing], that Allah is over all things capable." In one reading it is "Know!" (a'lam as an imperative), a command from Allah to him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 260:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when Abraham said: "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." He said﴾ (Allah, to him) ﴿"Have you not believed?"﴾ in My power to give life. He asked him this though he knew his belief in that, so that He would answer him with what he asked, and the listeners would know his purpose. ﴿He said: "Yes [I have believed], but﴾ [I asked] so that ﴿my heart may be at rest"﴾ [i.e., may be calm] ﴿through direct observation combined with reasoning.﴾ ﴿He said: "Take four birds and incline them toward you"﴾ with the sād vowelled with kasra or damma (ṣurhunna, i.e., incline or train them) toward you, ﴿then cut them into pieces and mix their flesh and feathers.﴾ So he took a peacock, a vulture, a crow and a rooster, did to them what was mentioned, and held their heads with himself and called them, and the parts flew to one another until they became complete, then they came to their heads. ﴿Then place on every mountain﴾ of the mountains of your land ﴿a portion of them; then call them﴾ to you, ﴿and they will come to you in haste.﴾ ﴿Swiftly.﴾ ﴿And know that Allah is Almighty﴾ nothing can overpower Him, ﴿Wise﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 261:

﴿Their likeness﴾ is the description of the expenditure of ﴿those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah﴾, i.e., in His obedience, ﴿is like a grain that sprouts seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains﴾. So their expenditure is multiplied seven hundredfold. ﴿And Allah multiplies﴾ it beyond that ﴿for whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing﴾ in His bounty, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of whoever deserves the multiplication.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 262:

﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and then do not follow what they have spent with reminders of their generosity [mannan] nor with injury [adha]—﴾ "Mannan" (reminding the recipient of one's favour): by their saying to the one they have spent upon, for example, "I have done you a kindness and mended your condition." ﴿Nor with injury﴾: nor by harming him through mentioning this to someone he dislikes having know of it, or the like. ﴿For them is their reward﴾: the reward of their spending ﴿with their Lord; no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 263:

﴿A kind word﴾ means a good speech and a gracious response to the one who asks. ﴿And forgiveness﴾ means forgiveness for him for his persistence (ilhah). ﴿Is better than charity followed by injury﴾ by reproach (mann) and by reproaching him for asking. ﴿And Allah is Free of need﴾ from the charity of the servants. ﴿Forbearing﴾ in delaying the punishment from the one who reproaches and injures.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 264:

﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities﴾ i.e., their rewards, ﴿with reminders or injury﴾ invalidating them through reminders and injury, ﴿like one who spends his wealth, [only] to be seen by the people﴾ i.e., like the invalidation of the expenditure of one who spends, showing off to them, ﴿and does not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾ he is the hypocrite. ﴿His example is like a smooth stone﴾ a bare, smooth rock, ﴿upon which is dust, and then a heavy rain strikes it﴾ a severe downpour, ﴿and leaves it bare﴾ hard and smooth, with nothing on it. ﴿They have no power over anything they have earned﴾ this is a resumption explaining the example of the hypocrite who spends to be seen by the people; the pronoun is pluralized in consideration of the meaning of "one who" (alladhi). ﴿That is, they find no reward for it in the Hereafter, just as nothing of the dust that was on the smooth rock remains on it after the rain has washed it away.﴾ ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 265:

﴿And the likeness﴾ (i.e., the likeness of the expenditure) of ﴿those who spend their wealth seeking﴾ (i.e., seeking) ﴿the pleasure of Allah and for the strengthening of their souls﴾ (i.e., for certainty of the reward for it), unlike the hypocrites, who do not hope for it because they deny it. The min here is ibtida'iyyah (indicating the starting point). ﴿Like a garden﴾ (i.e., an orchard) ﴿on a height﴾ (raba, with the ra' vowelled either with a damma or a fatha), a place elevated and level ﴿which a heavy rain has struck, so it brought forth﴾ (i.e., gave) ﴿its produce﴾ (ukul, with the kaf vowelled with a damma or with a sukun), meaning its fruit ﴿twofold﴾ (i.e., double) what other gardens produce. ﴿But if heavy rain does not strike it, then a light rain﴾ (a gentle rain that reaches it and suffices it because of its elevation). The meaning: it bears fruit and thrives whether the rain is abundant or scant; likewise the expenditure of those mentioned thrives with Allah, whether it is abundant or scant. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 266:

﴿Would one of you like﴾ (ayawaddu) i.e. would he love (ayuhibbu) ﴿that he should have a garden﴾ (jannah), i.e. an orchard, ﴿of palm trees and grapevines, beneath which rivers flow, and in which he has﴾ fruit ﴿of all kinds﴾ of produce, ﴿and﴾ (wa-qad) while ﴿old age has befallen him﴾, so that he has become weak from old age and unable to earn, ﴿and he has weak offspring﴾, i.e. small children who are unable to fend for themselves; ﴿then a whirlwind﴾, i.e. a strong wind, ﴿with fire in it strikes it and it is burnt up﴾, so he loses it at the very time he needs it most, and he and his children are left helpless and bewildered, with no means of recourse. This is a parable for the expenditure of one who shows off (al-murai) and one who reminds of his favours (al-mannan) when it goes to waste and does not benefit him, at the time when he needs it most in the Hereafter. The interrogative (al-istifham) here carries the sense of negation. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that this refers to a man who performed acts of obedience, then Satan sent to him, and he committed acts of disobedience until he burnt up his deeds. ﴿Thus﴾, as what has been mentioned has been made clear, ﴿God makes clear to you the signs, so that you may reflect﴾ (la'allakum tatafakkarun), and so take heed.

O you who have believed, spend (i.e., give zakat) of the good things you have earned, and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth (i.e., of grains and fruits). And do not aim at the bad (the inferior) of it to spend from it (i.e., from what was mentioned), spending it in zakat (this is a circumstantial clause, ḥāl, referring back to the pronoun in "tayammamū"), while you would not take it yourselves (i.e., the bad, if it were given to you as your due) unless you overlook it (by leniency and averting the eye). So how then would you pay God's right from it? And know that God is Self-Sufficient (independent of your expenditures), Praiseworthy (commendable in every state).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 268:

﴿The Shaitan threatens you with poverty﴾ he frightens you with it, if you give charity, so that you withhold. ﴿And he commands you to indecency﴾ stinginess and withholding the zakat. ﴿But Allah promises you﴾ for spending ﴿forgiveness from Him﴾ for your sins, ﴿and bounty﴾ provision, a replacement from Him. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing﴾ His bounty is vast, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of the one who spends.

Qur'an 2:269 is quoted as: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good.﴾ Then: ﴿And none will be mindful except those of understanding.﴾

Note: the Arabic tafsir text itself is the commentary and is translated below.

﴿Yu'ti al-hikmah﴾ (wisdom), i.e., beneficial knowledge that leads to action, ﴿man yasha'﴾ (to whom He wills), ﴿wa-man yu'ta al-hikmah fa-qad utiya khayran kathiran﴾ (and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good), because of its leading him to everlasting happiness. ﴿Wa-ma yudhdhakkar﴾ (and none will be mindful), in which the taa' in the original is assimilated into the dhal (idgham), meaning: takes heed, ﴿illa ulu al-albab﴾ (except those of understanding), i.e., possessors of intellects.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 270:

﴿Whatever expenditure you have spent﴾ [i.e., paid] as zakat or charity, ﴿or whatever vow you have vowed﴾ and fulfilled it, ﴿indeed Allah knows it﴾ and will reward you for it, ﴿and for the wrongdoers﴾ who withhold zakat and vows, or who place expenditure in other than its proper place, being acts of disobedience to Allah, ﴿there are no helpers﴾ preventing them from His punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 271:

﴿If you display﴾ [tubdū] means you make apparent, ﴿the charities﴾ [al-ṣadaqāt], i.e., the voluntary ones, ﴿then excellent is it﴾, i.e., excellent is the thing of their being displayed. ﴿And if you conceal them﴾ [tukhfūhā], you keep them secret, ﴿and give them to the poor, it is better for you﴾ than displaying them and giving them to the rich. As for obligatory charity (ṣadaqat al-far·d, the obligatory alms), displaying it is better, so that others may follow the example, and so that one is not accused (of withholding it); and giving it to the poor is required. ﴿And He will remove﴾ [wa-yukaffiru], with the verb in the third person (with yāʼ) and with nūn, read in the jussive by conjunction with the place of ﴿fa-huwa﴾, and in the nominative as a resumption (of the sentence) ﴿from you some﴾ [min] ﴿of your misdeeds [sayyiʼātikum]﴾. ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾, Knowing of its inward as of its outward, nothing of it being hidden from Him.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade giving charity to the polytheists so that they would embrace Islam, the verse was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾, i.e., to guide the people to entering Islam; upon you is only the conveyance (of the message). ﴿But Allah guides whom He wills﴾ to entering it. ﴿And whatever good you spend﴾ of wealth ﴿is for yourselves﴾, because its reward is for them. ﴿And you spend not except seeking the Face of Allah﴾, i.e., seeking His reward alone and not anything else of the worldly goods. It is a statement meaning a prohibition. ﴿And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you﴾, its recompense, ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾, i.e., you will not have anything of it diminished. The two clauses are an emphasis of the first.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 273:**

﴿For the poor﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., the charities (al-sadaqat). ﴿Who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾, i.e., they have confined themselves to jihad. It was revealed concerning the People of the Bench (Ahl al-Suffah), who were four hundred of the Emigrants (muhajirun) who were stationed to learn the Qur'an and to go out with the expeditions (al-sariyya). ﴿They cannot go about in the land﴾ travelling ﴿in the land﴾ for trade and livelihood, because they are occupied with jihad. ﴿The ignorant person thinks them wealthy because of their abstinence﴾ the one who is ignorant of their condition, ﴿because of their abstinence﴾, i.e., because of their restraint from asking and their refraining from it. ﴿You will recognize them﴾ O addressee ﴿by their mark﴾, their sign, from humility and the effect of exertion. ﴿They do not ask people﴾ for anything, so that they would press ﴿insistently﴾, i.e., they have no asking at all, so insistent pressing (al-ilhaf), which is persistence, does not occur from them. ﴿And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾, so He will reward you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 275:

﴿Those who consume ribā﴾, i.e., take it, and it is the increase in transactions involving money and foodstuffs, in quantity or in term. ﴿Will not stand﴾ from their graves ﴿except﴾ as standing ﴿like one whom Satan has driven to madness by touch﴾, i.e., has struck down, ﴿from the touch﴾, meaning madness. The phrase "from the touch" is connected to "will stand." ﴿That﴾, the state which has befallen them, ﴿is because﴾ due to the fact that ﴿they said: "Trade is only like ribā"﴾ in permissibility. This is an inverted comparison, for emphasis. Then Allah, exalted is He, answered them, saying: ﴿But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden ribā. So whoever has received an admonition﴾ reaching him ﴿from his Lord and desists﴾ from consuming it, ﴿he shall have what is past﴾, i.e., what preceded the prohibition; that is, he is not required to repay it, ﴿and his affair is up to Allah. But whoever returns﴾ to consuming it, likening it to trade in permissibility, ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 276:

﴿Allah diminishes usury﴾ (yamhaqu Allahu al-riba): He reduces it and removes its blessing. ﴿And makes charities grow﴾ (wa yurbi al-sadaqat): He increases them, causes them to grow, and multiplies their reward. ﴿And Allah does not love any ungrateful sinner﴾ (kulla kaffar): one who denies the lawfulness of usury by declaring it permitted; ﴿sinner﴾ (athim): one who is wicked (fajir) by consuming it, meaning He will punish him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 278:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due] from interest, if you should be believers.﴾ Leave (اُتْرُكُوا, utrukū) ﴿what remains [due] from interest﴾, being sincere in your faith, for it is among the qualities of the believer to comply with the command of Allah, the Exalted. It was revealed when some of the Companions demanded, after the prohibition, interest that they had been owed before.

﴿Then if you do not do it﴾ (i.e., what you were commanded), ﴿then be informed﴾ (i.e., know) ﴿of war from Allah and His Messenger﴾. In this there is a severe threat to them. When it was revealed, they said: "We have no power to wage war against Him." ﴿But if you repent﴾ (i.e., turn back from it), ﴿then you have your principal﴾ (uṣūl, the original sums) ﴿of your wealth; you do not wrong﴾ by adding interest, ﴿nor are you wronged﴾ by reduction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 280:

﴿And if the debtor is in hardship﴾, [if] a creditor [is] one who is in hardship, ﴿then let there be postponement﴾ to him, i.e., it is incumbent upon you to delay [the debt] ﴿until a time of ease﴾, with the sīn vocalized either with a fatḥah or a ḍammah, i.e., a time of ease. ﴿And that you give charity﴾, with tashdīd, based on the assimilation of the tā' in the original into the ṣād, and with takhfīf, based on its deletion, i.e., you give charity to the one in hardship by remitting [the debt], ﴿is better for you, if you only knew﴾ that it is better, so do it. And in a ḥadīth: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, or remits [the debt] for him, Allah will shade him in His shade on a day when there is no shade but His shade." Narrated by Muslim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 281:

﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah.﴾ With the passive voice (bi-l-binā' lil-maf'ūl), "turju'ūn" means "turadduna" (you will be brought back), and with the active voice (lil-fā'il) it means "tasīrūn" (you will proceed). ﴿In it, to Allah﴾ — that is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full﴾ in it ﴿for what it earned﴾, i.e., what it did of good and evil, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ by any reduction of a good deed or any increase in an evil deed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 282:

﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt⁠—﴾ you deal ﴿with a debt⁠—﴾ such as a salam (advance sale) or a loan ﴿for a specified term⁠—﴾ known ﴿write it down.⁠﴾ Write it down for the sake of securing it and averting dispute.

﴿And let a scribe write it between you in justice⁠—﴾ in truth, in his writing; he should not increase the principal or the term, nor decrease them. ﴿And let no scribe refuse⁠—﴾ abstain ﴿to write it, as Allah has taught him⁠—﴾ i.e., has favoured him with the skill of writing; so let him not withhold it. The kaf (as) is connected to "yaʾba" (refuse). ﴿So let him write⁠—﴾ emphasis. ﴿And let the one who has the obligation dictate⁠—﴾ the debtor, ﴿because he is the one against whom testimony is given, so that he acknowledges it and it is known what is owed upon him. ﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord⁠—﴾ in his dictation ﴿and not diminish⁠—﴾ reduce ﴿from it⁠—﴾ i.e., from the debt ﴿anything. But if the one who has the obligation is foolish⁠—﴾ wasteful ﴿or weak⁠—﴾ unable to dictate ﴿due to youth or old age, or is unable to dictate himself⁠—﴾ due to muteness, or ignorance of the language, or the like ﴿then let his guardian dictate in justice⁠—﴾ the one who manages his affairs, such as a father, a legal executor, a guardian, or a translator.

﴿And call in to witness two witnesses from among your men⁠—﴾ i.e., adult Muslim free men ﴿and if there are not two men, then a man and two women⁠—﴾ who testify ﴿from among those whom you accept as witnesses⁠—﴾ for their religion and their uprightness. The multiplicity of women is for the sake of ﴿that if one of them errs⁠—﴾ forgets ﴿one of them⁠—﴾ the testimony, due to the deficiency of their intellect and retentiveness ﴿then one of them will remind⁠—﴾ with light and emphatic pronunciation ﴿the other⁠—﴾ the one who remembers, ﴿the other⁠—﴾ the forgetful one. The clause of reminding is the place of the cause, i.e., so that she may remember if she errs, and it is introduced by "in case of error" because error is its cause. In another reading, "an" is conditional with a kasra, and the raising of "tudhakkir" is a resumption of its apodosis.

﴿And let no witness refuse when they are called⁠—﴾ "idha ma" is superfluous; they are called to bear and to give testimony. ﴿And do not be weary of writing it⁠—﴾ i.e., what you testified to of the right, due to how often this occurs, ﴿whether it is small⁠—﴾ little ﴿or large⁠—﴾ much ﴿up to its term⁠—﴾ the time of its falling due; this is a circumstantial clause relating to the pronoun in "tuktubuhu" (write it). ﴿That⁠—﴾ i.e., the writing ﴿is more just⁠—﴾ more equitable ﴿with Allah, and more upright for testimony⁠—﴾ i.e., more helpful in establishing it, since it reminds them of it ﴿and nearer to⁠—﴾ closer to ﴿avoiding⁠—﴾ that you not ﴿doubt⁠—﴾ be uncertain about the amount of the right and the term.

﴿Except that it be a present trade⁠—﴾ occurring ﴿which you conduct among yourselves⁠—﴾ i.e., you take possession of it with no term in it. ﴿Then there is no blame upon you⁠—﴾ in ﴿not writing it.⁠﴾ What is meant by it is that which is decided on the spot. ﴿And call witnesses when you conclude a sale⁠—﴾ regarding it, for that is more effective in preventing disagreement. This and what precedes it is a command of recommendation.

﴿Let no scribe or witness be harmed⁠—﴾ by the right-holder or the one against whom it lies, through distortion or refusal to witness or write, and the right-holder should not harm them by assigning them what is unbecoming in writing and testimony. ﴿And if you do⁠—﴾ what you have been forbidden ﴿then it is a transgression⁠—﴾ departure from obedience ﴿that clings to you. And fear Allah⁠—﴾ regarding His command and prohibition. ﴿And Allah teaches you⁠—﴾ the interests of your affairs; a circumstantial clause, or a resumed sentence. ﴿And Allah is Knower of all things.⁠﴾

﴿And if you are on a journey﴾, i.e., travelling, ﴿and you contract a debt but do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken into possession﴾, by which you secure your rights. The Sunnah (the established practice and teaching of the Prophet ﷺ) clarified the permissibility of the pledge (rahn, a security given to the creditor against a debt) while at home, and [also clarified] the existence of a scribe. The restriction to what is mentioned [in the verse] is because documentation in that case is stronger. In one recitation (qira'ah, a canonically transmitted mode of reciting the Qur'an), the word فَرِهان is read as the plural of رَهْن (rahn). The phrase ﴿taken into possession﴾ (مَقْبُوضَة) indicates the condition that the pledge must be taken into possession, and that possession by the pledgee (al-murtahin, the creditor) or his agent is sufficient.

﴿Then if one of you trusts another﴾, i.e., the creditor trusts the debtor for his right and so does not take a pledge, ﴿let the one who has been entrusted﴾, i.e., the debtor, ﴿discharge his trust﴾, i.e., his debt, ﴿and let him fear Allah, his Lord﴾ in discharging it. ﴿And do not conceal testimony﴾ when you are called to establish it. ﴿And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾. The heart is singled out for mention because it is the seat of testimony, and because when it sins, others who follow it are also sinful, and so they are punished with the punishment of sinners. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾, nothing of it being hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 284:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you show what is in your souls﴾ (tuzhirū) ﴿of evil and resolve upon it, or conceal it﴾ (tusirrūhu), ﴿Allah will call you to account for it﴾ (yukhbirukum), i.e., inform you of it on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and He will forgive whom He wills﴾ forgiveness for him, ﴿and punish whom He wills﴾ punishment for him. The two verbs in the jussive (yuḥāsibkum and what follows) are coordinated with the answer of the conditional, and the nominative reading means: so He (fa-huwa) [forgives and punishes]. ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾, and among that is His calling you to account and His recompense for you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 285:

﴿The Messenger believed﴾ [āmana] means he affirmed (ṣaddaqa), Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿in what was sent down to him from his Lord﴾ of the Qur'an, ﴿and the believers﴾ [wa'l-mu'minūna], conjoined to it (ʿuṭifa ʿalayhi), ﴿all﴾ [kull], its tanwīn being a replacement (ʿiwaḍ) for the genitive noun that was added to (al-muḍāf ilayhi), ﴿believed in God and His angels and His books﴾ [with the plural and the singular readings], ﴿and His messengers﴾, saying, ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾, so that we believe in some and disbelieve in others as the Jews and Christians did. ﴿And they say: We hear﴾, i.e., we accept what we have been commanded to accept by hearing (samāʿ qabūl), ﴿and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord﴾, we ask Your forgiveness, our Lord, ﴿and to You is the final return﴾, the place of return (al-marjiʿ) at the Resurrection. When the verse before it was revealed, the believers complained of the whisperings (al-waswasa) and the reckoning for them was hard upon them, so this was revealed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 2, verse 286:

﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ i.e., what its power can bear. ﴿It earns what it has earned﴾ — it earns of good, i.e., its reward. ﴿And it bears what it has earned﴾ — of evil, i.e., its burden. No one is held to account for another's sin, nor for what he did not earn of what his soul whispered to him. ﴿Say: "Our Lord, do not hold us accountable"﴾ with punishment ﴿if we forget or make mistakes﴾, i.e., abandon what is right, not deliberately, as You held accountable those before us. Allah has lifted this from this community, as is related in the hadith. So their asking is an acknowledgment of Allah's blessing. ﴿"Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden (iṣr)"﴾ — a matter whose carrying is heavy upon us. ﴿As You placed it upon those before us﴾, i.e., the Children of Israel: killing oneself in repentance, giving a quarter of one's wealth in zakat, and cutting off the place of impurity. ﴿"Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability (qudrah) to bear"﴾ from obligations and trials. ﴿"And pardon us"﴾ — wipe out our sins. ﴿"And forgive us and have mercy upon us"﴾ — mercy is an addition to forgiveness. ﴿"You are our Protector (mawlana)"﴾ — our Master and the one who manages our affairs. ﴿"So help us against the disbelieving people"﴾ — by establishing the proof and victory in fighting them, for it is among the nature of a protector to help his allies against enemies. And in the hadith: (When this verse was revealed and he ﷺ recited it, it was said to him after every phrase: "Indeed, I have done it.")
